title: Create unified ability parser in universal/
description:
Multiple parsers independently parse abilities from HTML: creatures (process_interaction_ability), monster families (parse_ability_nodes in change_extraction.py), monster templates (same), and feats/skills also need it. Each implementation handles addons, traits, actions, and afflictions differently (or not at all — the family parser doesn't handle any of them properly). Create a single universal_parse_abilities() function in universal/ that: 1. Takes raw BeautifulSoup nodes (NOT pre-processed text) 2. Splits on /
boundaries to identify ability entries 3. Extracts name + optional link from or tags 4. Extracts action_type from elements 5. Extracts traits from parenthesized text at description start 6. Merges addon fields (Requirements, Effect, Trigger, Frequency, Cost, Duration, Critical Success/Failure, etc.) into preceding ability 7. Detects affliction patterns (Saving Throw + Stage N) and restructures as affliction objects All parsers (creatures, monster families, monster templates, feats, skills) should call this instead of their own implementations. The content filters should NOT unwrap action spans — the unified parser needs them intact. Prerequisite: stop unwrapping action spans in monster_family._content_filter and monster_template._content_filter.
notes: Analysis complete. 7 parsers with 5 different action type implementations, 3 trait approaches, 3 addon/bold field approaches. Only creatures handle afflictions. Key shared functions already exist: extract_action_type (action.py), extract_starting_traits (trait.py), extract_bold_fields (universal.py). The unified parser needs to combine all of these and add affliction detection. Parsers to update: creatures, monster_families, monster_templates, feats, skills.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete in PR #94. universal/ability.py created, monster families (191/191) and templates (55/55) migrated. Creature and feat/skill migration tracked separately in PFSRD2-Parser-ob6w and PFSRD2-Parser-91hd.

title: Remove default None from group_subtype parameter
description:
Line 941: Function signature has group_subtype=None default, making it unclear if parameter is required or optional. This hides whether callers need to provide this value.

Strategic fragility: No default - force caller to be explicit. Pass None at call site if not needed.
close_reason: Removed default None parameter. All equipment types parse successfully with no errors or data changes.

title: Remove defensive .get('group_subtype') hiding config errors
description:
Line 469: Using .get('group_subtype') with default None hides configuration errors. If group_subtype is required for an equipment type but missing from config, we silently pass None instead of failing fast.

Strategic fragility: Force callers to pass group_subtype explicitly or use config['group_subtype'] to fail on missing config.
close_reason: Replaced defensive .get() with explicit fail-fast check. All equipment types parse successfully with no errors or data changes.

title: Remove defensive type check in ammunition normalization
description:
Line 1996-1997: isinstance(html_str, dict) check with comment 'shouldn't be, but be defensive'. This hides bugs where ammunition is already a dict. Remove the check and let it fail with TypeError if html_str is not a string.

Strategic fragility: If ammunition is already a dict, that's a bug that should fail loudly, not be silently skipped.
close_reason: Removed defensive isinstance check. All equipment types parse successfully with no errors or data changes.

title: LLM enrichment picked the wrong damage in 8 abilities; 12 more capture only part of a scaled ladder
description:
LLM enrichment: 36 hand-validated ambiguous damage picks

Scope. 808 LLM-derived ability records supply 1580 field values. All of them
now pass the grounding guard (every number, damage type and save type appears
in the ability's own source text). Grounding cannot catch the model choosing
the WRONG value from among several the text offers, so the 1203 damage/save
values were partitioned by whether a choice existed: 891 had 0-1 candidates,
152 took every die present, 160 involved a real choice. Of those 160, 102 drop
only non-damage dice (recharge timers, durations, table rolls). The remaining
36 were hand-checked. Verdicts follow.

=== A. WRONG: took a secondary value and dropped the primary (8) ===

Shell Rake, ability_id 116 and 11752                      SHIPPED in baomal.json
  Text: "takes 6d6+10 slashing and piercing damage (DC 42 basic Reflex)".
  Took 3d6+5, which is the against-vessels variant. The primary damage is gone.

Sapping Squeeze, ability_id 3128                          SHIPPED in shanrigol_heap.json
  Text: "dealing 1d6+5 bludgeoning and 1d4 persistent bleed damage".
  Took only the 1d4 bleed. The primary bludgeoning is gone.

Sapping Squeeze, ability_id 3132                          SHIPPED in shanrigol_behemoth.json
  Text: "dealing 1d10+11 bludgeoning and 1d6 persistent bleed damage".
  Took only the 1d6 bleed. Same defect, same ability, different creature.

Breath Weapon, ability_id 2010
  Text: "deals 12d6 negative energy damage ... Undead creatures take 14d6
  force damage instead of the negative damage."
  Took 14d6 force -- the undead-only alternative -- and dropped the 12d6 that
  applies to everyone else.

Stampede, ability_id 10187                                SHIPPED in aurochs_herd.json
  Text: "the bludgeoning damage increases to 4d6+6 (prone creatures take
  5d6+6 bludgeoning damage instead)."
  Took 5d6+6, the prone-only case, and dropped the 4d6+6 general case.

Pack Attack, ability_id 7433                              SHIPPED in nornhound.json
  Text: "Strikes deal 1d6 extra damage ... Swallow Whole (attack); Huge,
  3d12+10 bludgeoning, Rupture 36"
  Took 3d12+10, which belongs to Swallow Whole -- a DIFFERENT ability whose
  text was adjacent. Cross-check: every other Pack Attack in the corpus deals
  1d4 to 3d6; this one alone is 3d12+10.

Dragon's Wisdom, ability_id 3147
  Text: "deal 4d6 extra damage of that [type]". Took 21d6, which appears
  elsewhere in the merged text.

=== B. INCOMPLETE: action- or size-scaled ladder, partially captured (12) ===

These publish a subset of a list where every entry is real. Not wrong values,
but a consumer reading them gets one rung of a ladder with no indication the
others exist.

  Claws, Fangs, and Horns (7289)   took 3d10+12, left 1d10+12 and 2d10+12
  Beaks, Claws, and Talons (7295)  took 3d12+14, left 1d12+14 and 2d12+14
  Rain of Spears (9821)            took the whole piercing ladder and dropped
                                   the entire electricity ladder (1d12/2d12/3d12)
  Jaws and Claws (10599)           took only the persistent bleed; dropped the
                                   primary slashing ladder entirely
  Morningstar Massacre (10585)     took 2 of 3 rungs
  Thrashing Vines (10608)          took 4 values, left 1d6 and 3d6
  dwarven longshots (10622, 17448) took 2 of 3 rungs
  Regurgitate (207)                size ladder Tiny..Huge; took only Huge
  Change Shape (254, 8378)         multi-form list; took 2 of 4 forms
  Modular Arms (5768)              took 5, left 1d6

=== C. DEFENSIBLE: the model chose correctly (16) ===

  Generate Bomb (740, 8925)   the dropped 1d6 is the chamber table roll
  Dirt Breath (5770)          3d6 is the damage; the rest are unrelated
  Artistic Destruction (9884) 8d6 is the damage; 1d4 is a recharge
  Splinter Breath (10088)     4d6 base; 2d6 is a per-head increment
  Focused Assault (305)       1d8 per extra weapon; 5d8 is the cap
  Focused Flames (1904)       2d6 per knife; 6d6 is the cap
  Caustic Pustules (16076)    1d6 base; 2d6/3d6 are level scaling
  Field of Slaughter (10219)  3d6 base; 3d6+3 is a conditional variant
  Whirlwind Form (1289)       both real damage types captured
  Osseous Defense (5601)      spike and dart damage captured
  Dance of Ruin (285)         both rungs captured
  Telekinetic Storm (1079, 4564, 4668, 9005)
                              spread-vs-focused variants; base taken

=== Separate finding ===

ability_id 10622 and 17448 are NAMED "Frequency once per round". That is a
parser bug -- a Frequency line was consumed as the ability name. Unrelated to
enrichment; worth its own ticket.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
CORRECTION: Pack Attack was never an LLM error. It is an HTML bug, now fixed.

nornhound's Swallow Whole was appended inside Pack Attack's
<span class="hanging-indent"> rather than opening its own, and was not bolded.
The parser read one ability where there are two, so Pack Attack's text ran
through Swallow Whole's entire stat line and the enricher was handed both
abilities as one blob. It picked the wrong one's dice. No prompt or schema
could have fixed that; the input was wrong.

    before   Pack Attack   damage 3d12+10   (Swallow Whole's)
             Swallow Whole empty stub
    after    Pack Attack   damage 1d6       (its own)
             Swallow Whole action One Action, its own text

Fixed in PFSRD2-Web (7b0cb965e8, branch fix/nornhound-swallow-whole-span) and
verified by reparse. Checked against the corpus rather than assumed: 87 Swallow
Whole stat-block entries open their own bolded span and this was the only one
that did not.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE REST OF THIS TICKET. The eight "wrong damage" cases
need re-triage, because two different diagnoses have now proved wrong:

  1. Several were STALE, not mis-selected. Re-querying qwen2.5:7b with the
     CURRENT prompt returns the correct value for Shell Rake, Breath Weapon,
     Dragon's Wisdom and Sapping Squeeze -- the stored data came from an older
     prompt revision. See PFSRD2-Parser-4k8b.
  2. This one was malformed input.

So the count of genuine model mis-selections is smaller than eight and may be
zero. Do not act on the original list without re-deriving it. The right
sequence is: fix any remaining HTML, re-enrich with the current prompt at
temperature 0, and only then see what is still wrong.

Worth generalising: every time a damage value looked wrong in this ticket and
was traced to the end, the cause was upstream of the model -- a stale prompt, a
merged span, a deferred DC the source never published. The maintainer's rule
that AoN data is riven with HTML mistakes has held every time it was tested.

title: Lexical filename sort makes the OLDER AoN page win when IDs differ in digit count (8 monsters)
description:
AoN publishes a reprint as a NEW object with a HIGHER aonid, and the newer object is meant to override the lower one. When two pages write the same output filename, the intended winner is the higher ID. That is working as designed and is documented in CLAUDE.md.

It breaks when the two IDs have different digit counts.

The creature driver iterates `ls Monsters.aspx.ID_*.html`, which sorts LEXICALLY. "ID_1422" sorts BEFORE "ID_430" because '1' < '4'. So the newer page is written first and the OLDER page is written last and wins.

  $ ls | grep -E "ID_(430|1422)\."
  Monsters.aspx.ID_1422.html      <- newer, written first
  Monsters.aspx.ID_430.html       <- older, written LAST, wins

8 monster files currently hold the older version. The symptom is self-identifying: each carries AoN's own note link saying "There is a more recent version of this monster" pointing at an aonid HIGHER than its own.

  monsters/pathfinder_145_hellknight_hill/anadi_hunter.json     430  <- newer 1422
  monsters/pathfinder_145_hellknight_hill/anadi_sage.json       431  <- newer 1423
  monsters/pathfinder_146_cult_of_cinders/biloko_warrior.json   441  <- newer 1427
  monsters/pathfinder_146_cult_of_cinders/eloko.json            443  <- newer 1429
  monsters/the_mwangi_expanse/anadi_hunter.json                 430  <- newer 1422
  monsters/the_mwangi_expanse/anadi_sage.json                   431  <- newer 1423
  monsters/the_mwangi_expanse/biloko_warrior.json               441  <- newer 1427
  monsters/the_mwangi_expanse/eloko.json                        443  <- newer 1429

This is not cosmetic. Regenerating these files changes real statistics, because the older printing genuinely differs:

  anadi_sage        AC 20 -> 21, Ref +11 -> +10, Will +14 -> +12,
                    spell DC 21 -> 22, venom DC 19 -> 20
  biloko_warrior    loses a flavour paragraph, TWO Shield Block automatic
                    abilities with their links, low-light vision, and scent

DETECTOR (cheap, and the one used to find these):

  a file whose own aonid is LOWER than the aonid in any "more recent version"
  note link it carries

FIX: sort the driver's file list numerically on the ID, not lexically. One
change in bin/, and it makes "higher ID wins" true rather than
true-when-the-digits-line-up.

RELATED BUT A DIFFERENT CAUSE. The same detector also finds two NPC files:

  npcs/monster_core_2/tripkee_scout.json   3673  <- newer 4589
  npcs/npc_core/tripkee_scout.json         3673  <- newer 4589

Those digit counts MATCH, so sorting is not the cause. NPCs.aspx.ID_4589.html
is simply not present in pfsrd2-web -- the newer page was never scraped. That is
a download-completeness problem, not a parser one, and probably wants its own
ticket once someone confirms whether the page exists upstream.

HISTORY: PFSRD2-Parser-q389 reported the shared-filename behaviour as
non-determinism and was correctly closed as not-a-bug, because the case examined
there (boggard_scout, 2856 vs 4000) has matching digit counts and resolves the
right way. The digit-count caveat was recorded on that ticket as an unverified
question. This is that case, verified.

All 10 files are held unstaged and are NOT in the data commits on
feature/hazard-degree-effects.

title: Deferred DCs materialised as static numbers: 16 dragon abilities, DC 20 where the source says 28/33/40
description:
monster_families/monster_core/dragon_adamantine.json ships a saving throw the source never published:

  ability: Repelling Blast (sections[6].abilities[3])
  emitted: {"basic": true, "dc": 30, "save_type": "Ref",
            "subtype": "save_dc", "text": "DC 30 basic Reflex"}

What the source actually says (pfsrd2-web/2e.aonprd.com/MonsterFamilies/MonsterFamilies.aspx.ID_396.html):

  "Creatures in the area take slashing damage equal to the dragon's Avalanche
   Breath (with a basic Reflex save of the same DC)."

There is no number. The DC is explicitly deferred to another ability's DC.

Proof it is not derived from anywhere legitimate:
  * "DC 30" does not occur anywhere in the source HTML. Every literal "30" in
    that file is inside an SVG viewbox attribute or a JavaScript date-format
    string.
  * The other DCs in the family are 20, 28, 34, 41 and 44. None is 30, and
    none combines to 30.
  * git show HEAD:...dragon_adamantine.json has zero occurrences of "dc": 30.
    The value appears only after a current-parser run.
  * The enrichment DB has two ability_records named "Repelling Blast"
    (ability_id 16150 and 17662); BOTH have saving_throw = null. Not from the DB.
  * There is no "Avalanche Breath" ability in this file to inherit a DC from.

Probable cause, needs confirming: the string "DC 30 basic Reflex" is a verbatim
few-shot exemplar inside the LLM enrichment prompt.

  pfsrd2/enrichment/llm_extractor.py:202
      - "DC 30 Fortitude save" or "DC 30 basic Reflex"
  pfsrd2/enrichment/llm_extractor.py:213-214
      Text: "DC 30 basic Reflex save. It can't use Breath Weapon again for 1d4 rounds."
      Result: DC 30 basic Reflex

The emitted text is character-for-character that exemplar. On an input whose DC
is "the same DC" — i.e. absent — the model appears to have echoed its own
example instead of returning nothing. That is the classic few-shot contamination
failure, and it produces game data that looks entirely plausible.

I checked the other five files in pfsrd2-data containing the exact string
"DC 30 basic Reflex" and they are all LEGITIMATE — each one's source really does
publish DC 30:
  monsters/rage_of_elements/oregorger.json            (Searing Spew)
  monsters/malevolence/algea.json                     (Frenzied Beaks)
  monsters/pathfinder_189_.../ilakni.json             (Blackfrost Breath)
  monsters/bestiary/adult_red_dragon.json             (Dragon Heat, aonid 137: "5 feet, DC 30 basic Reflex")
  monsters/monster_core_2/adult_cinder_dragon.json    (Dragon Heat, aonid 4346: "5 feet, DC 30 basic Reflex, 3d6 fire damage")
So this is one instance, not a systemic flood -- but one fabricated DC is one
too many, and the mechanism that produced it would produce more.

SUGGESTED WORK
 1. Confirm the LLM path is what emits it (run the extractor on the Repelling
    Blast effect text in isolation).
 2. Change the exemplars in DC_PROMPT to values that cannot be mistaken for
    real data, or better, make the prompt's examples abstract.
 3. Add a guard: a DC extracted by the LLM whose digits do not appear in the
    input text is rejected. That is cheap, and it turns a silent fabrication
    into a loud failure.
 4. Sweep the corpus for other LLM-extracted values whose digits are absent
    from their source text.

Found while reviewing PR #175's data diff file by file. dragon_adamantine.json
is held unstaged. Not caused by #175 -- the file's degree fold is correct; this
surfaced because the ability was split into Repelling Blast and Scything Wings,
which put the effect text through the enrichment path.
notes:
MAINTAINER (2026-08-17): "the adamantine dragon's family's optional ability really should not have added that DC, since the DC is expressly the DC of the dragon it is applied to's breath weapon dc"

That reframes this and makes it much bigger than one hallucinated number. The
DC is DEFERRED BY DESIGN. No static value is correct, because the ability is
applied to whichever dragon takes it, and each has its own breath DC. So the
right output is no DC at all, not a better-guessed DC.

Swept the corpus for the whole class: an ability whose text expressly defers its
DC ("DC equal to...", "of the same DC", "the DC of...") that nonetheless carries
a static saving_throw whose number does not appear in that text.

  16 instances.

PROOF THAT THE STATIC VALUE IS WRONG, not merely unsupported. Cratering Smash
says "a Reflex save with a DC equal to the dragon's Avalanche Breath". All three
adamantine dragons ship the same DC while their breath DCs differ:

  monsters/monster_core/young_adamantine_dragon.json    Cratering Smash DC 20   Avalanche Breath DC 28
  monsters/monster_core/adult_adamantine_dragon.json    Cratering Smash DC 20   Avalanche Breath DC 33
  monsters/monster_core/ancient_adamantine_dragon.json  Cratering Smash DC 20   Avalanche Breath DC 40

The correct values are 28/33/40. 20 is wrong for every one of them.

FULL LIST (ability -> emitted DC):

  Cratering Smash   DC 20   monster_families/monster_core/dragon_adamantine.json
                            monsters/monster_core/{young,adult,ancient}_adamantine_dragon.json
                            monsters/draconic_codex/adamantine_archdragon.json
  Cloud of Ashes    DC 30   monster_families/monster_core_2/dragon_cinder.json
                            monsters/monster_core_2/{young,adult,ancient}_cinder_dragon.json
                            monsters/draconic_codex/cinder_archdragon.json
  Shred Souls       DC 20   monster_families/monster_core_2/dragon_resurrection.json
                            monsters/monster_core_2/{young,adult,ancient}_resurrection_dragon.json
                            monsters/draconic_codex/resurrection_archdragon.json
  Repelling Blast   DC 30   monster_families/monster_core/dragon_adamantine.json

NEW vs PRE-EXISTING -- checked against c2e82f0c0~1, the state before this
branch's data commits:

  Repelling Blast DC 30   NEW. The base has saving_throw absent entirely. This
                          is the one PR #175 introduced, via the ability split
                          that put the effect text through the enrichment path,
                          and it is the one whose value matches the LLM prompt's
                          few-shot example verbatim.
  the other 15            PRE-EXISTING. Already shipped in committed data before
                          this branch. Not caused by e01u.

So the LLM few-shot contamination described below is real and is responsible for
exactly one of the sixteen. The other fifteen are a standing defect: something in
the pipeline materialises a deferred DC into a static number.

REVISED SUGGESTED WORK

 1. A deferred DC must produce NO saving_throw value. The LLM prompt already
    says "Do NOT extract: References to another creature's DC" -- so the prompt
    anticipated this and the model did it anyway, which is an argument for a
    deterministic guard rather than better prompting.
 2. Guard: reject any extracted DC whose digits do not occur in the source text
    for that ability. That catches all 16 mechanically, and would have caught
    Repelling Blast at parse time.
 3. Separately decide whether a deferred DC should be MODELLED as a reference
    (e.g. save_dc with a `derived_from` naming the ability) rather than dropped.
    Dropping is honest; a reference is more useful; inventing is what happens now.
 4. Change the DC_PROMPT exemplars so a regurgitated example is not a plausible
    game value.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
RESOLVED. Closing after verifying the class is gone, not just the instance.

Root cause was as suspected in the description: few-shot contamination. The
string "DC 30 basic Reflex" is a verbatim exemplar in DC_PROMPT, and on an input
whose DC is deferred ("a basic Reflex save of the same DC") the model echoed its
own example.

What shipped as the fix (PR #175, merged as 3df91ff):

  a_number_the_source_never_published rejects any number in an LLM answer that
  does not occur in the text the model was given. Deterministic, needs no
  judgement, and cannot be fixed by better prompting -- a model cannot invent a
  number that is already in its input.

  The guard runs on BOTH LLM paths. It first existed only on the inline
  enricher, which covered 6 of the 63 poisoned records; the other 57 came
  through bin/pf2_enrich_abilities run_llm, an identical extractor loop with no

title: Repeated addon label silently overwrites: 13 files lose published text
description:
universal/ability.py:_apply_addon ends in `ability[key] = value`. If a label appears twice on one ability the second value silently overwrites the first, and the earlier published text exists nowhere in the output. No error, valid schema. Adding the one-line guard assert key not in ability, ( f"{ability.get('name')!r} publishes {addon_name!r} twice; the second " f"value would overwrite {ability[key]!r}" ) surfaces 13 files with real, ALREADY-SHIPPED loss. It was written and validated during PR #165, then removed from that PR because 13 failing files violates the zero-errors policy and the fixes are a separate concern from that PR's subject. The guard should land together with the fixes below. FAILING FILES (13) MonsterFamilies.aspx.ID_396 'Repelling Blast' publishes 'Effect' twice MonsterFamilies.aspx.ID_585 'Afterimage Jumps' publishes 'Frequency' twice Hazards.aspx.ID_45, 48, 282, 351, 382, 393, 458, 487, 488, 568, 609 None are caused by PR #165. The two family cases are Effect/Frequency, which were already in DEFAULT_ADDON_LABELS before that PR; hazards already had the degree labels. A full creature run (3670 files) fires the assert ZERO times, so creatures are clean. DIAGNOSED EXAMPLE — Hazards ID_45 (gm_core/confounding_betrayal) Bold sequence in the source: Unmask ... Trigger ... Critical Success ... Success ... Critical Failure ... Routine ... Critical Success ... Success ... Critical Failure ... There are two degree runs. The first belongs to the Unmask reaction; the second belongs to the Routine's save. `Routine` is a hazard FIELD_LABEL, extracted separately rather than starting a new ability, so the Unmask ability is still open when the second run arrives and swallows it. Shipped result in hazards/gm_core/confounding_betrayal.json: Unmask carries the SECOND critical_success ("The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune for 1 minute."), and the first ("The creature sees through the illusions entirely and is temporarily immune to the haunt's routine for 1 minute.") appears nowhere in the file. So the real hazard defect is that a degree run following a field label is attributed to the previous ability. Fixing that probably fixes most or all of the 11 hazard cases; the 2 family cases need their own look (likely missing
in the source, i.e. HTML bugs). WORK 1. investigate each of the 13: HTML bug (fix pfsrd2-web) vs parser bug (fix code) 2. land the assert once they parse clean 3. re-run hazards and families and review the recovered text in the data diff Found by strategic-fragility-reviewer on PR #165, comment 3790798599.

title: Composite item references: address '+1 striking shock longsword' as a thing
description:
THE KEYSTONE PROBLEM. A composite item — a base item plus potency plus fundamental and property runes, optionally of a precious material — has no identity anywhere in the data. It is not a document, has no game-id, and cannot be linked to. Consumers can only see the name string.

What exists today, in stat_block.gear (1856 creatures, 5433 entries):

- 4747 entries carry links, so the PARTS are often addressable: '+1 striking longsword' resolves to striking (Equipment 280) and longsword (Weapons 31).
- 1181 entries begin with a potency bonus and the potency is NEVER linked. The '+1' lives only in the name string, even though Weapon Potency and Armor Potency are real documents with per-grade variants.
- AoN's own link granularity is inconsistent: the same concept appears as 'striking', '1 striking' and '+1 striking' across entries.
- 1107 rune-bearing entries do already have a resolved base item, so the raw material is better than it looks.

The consequence: nothing can answer 'what does this creature's weapon actually do'. The rune effects work (PFSRD2-Parser-dsx1) can compute what a shock rune adds, but there is no addressable thing to add it TO.

This is also why specific magic items are stuck — see the sibling ticket on weapon facts.
design:
A composite is a RECIPE over addressable parts, not a document to synthesise. Combinatorially there are millions; do not generate them.

Proposed shape on a gear entry, beside the existing name and links rather than replacing them:

  item_reference: {
    base: { game-id, game-obj, name },      # longsword
    potency: 1,                              # from the name string; Weapon Potency variant is addressable
    fundamental: [ { game-id, name, grade } ],   # striking / greater striking
    property: [ { game-id, name } ],             # shock, flaming
    material: { game-id, name } | null,          # cold iron, mithral
    quantity: 1
  }

Parse from the name string, validate against the existing links rather than trusting either alone — the links are the ground truth for identity, the name string is the ground truth for potency and ordering. Where they disagree, that is a source or parser bug worth surfacing, not silently reconciling.

Never invent a part that is not in the name. An unparseable gear string keeps its name and gets needs_review.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can take a creature's gear entry and resolve every component to a game-id, including the potency grade; the 1181 potency-bearing entries carry a numeric potency; disagreements between name and links are reported rather than guessed; unparseable entries are flagged not fabricated.

title: Executable item effects: make runes change the item they are etched on
description:
Today only 22 fundamental/reinforcing rune grades carry executable effects (46 effect objects across 13 documents). All 141 property runes ship prose only, so a +1 striking shock longsword does not add its 1d6 electricity anywhere a consumer can read it.

The survey behind this epic (2026-08-15) found the property runes are not one problem but four, with very different costs:

1. UNCONDITIONAL ON-HIT DAMAGE — 18 documents (~10 runes x 2 editions): Shock, Flaming, Frost, Corrosive, Thundering, Astral, Brilliant, Decaying, Disrupting, Impactful, Nightmare, Unholy. Text is highly regular ('deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a successful Strike'). Needs no new schema: append an attack_damage entry, a shape that already ships on creatures.

2. CONDITIONAL EFFECTS — the vocabulary gap. Bane and Giant-Killing are creature-type gated; Energy-Resistant grants a resistance the CRAFTER CHOOSES; crit riders fire only on a critical hit. All three need a condition qualifier on the effect, and the crafter-choice case needs the engine's existing but unused 'select' operation.

3. ACTIVATED ABILITIES — 17 property runes mention activation and ZERO of 141 carry any structured activation data. Activation is generally an action, so the honest model is that the item grants an action: the same ability shape with an action_type that creatures already use. This is wider than runes — every activatable item has the same gap.

4. NOT MECHANICAL — roughly 50 weapon and 33 armor runes are rule overrides or narrative (Ghost Touch's targeting rule, Misleading's flat-check DC, Fortification's crit-to-hit conversion). These keep their prose and get needs_review. Never fabricate an effect.

Armor is the more heterogeneous half and was under-examined before this survey: 43 property runes, of which only a handful are passive numeric changes.
design:
Do tier 1 first because it needs no schema change and proves the pipeline end to end. Tier 2 is one design decision (a condition qualifier) that unlocks type-gating, crit-gating and crafter choice together — do not solve them separately. Tier 3 is a different shape entirely and should not hide inside the rune work.

Reference implementations already in the corpus: attack_damage with persistent:true ships 564 times on creatures; a damage entry with notes 'on a critical hit' ships twice; condition riders ship as modifier entries with a Conditions link; the damage types runes need (spirit 220, evil 204, good 66, holy 1) are all proven.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can ask 'what damage does this runed weapon do' and get an answer for the tier-1 runes; tier-2 conditions are expressible without fabricating; activation is tracked separately; everything else keeps prose plus needs_review.
notes:
Children (bd cannot model epic->task membership as a dependency, so recorded here):

  j1w3  Composite item references — THE KEYSTONE. Nothing else delivers user-visible
        value without it, because there is no addressable thing to apply effects to.
  vu32  Weapon facts on specific magic weapons — 277 items have no weapon_modes,
        so eligibility and damage cannot be computed for them.
  vqjp  Tier 1: on-hit damage for the 18 unconditional runes. Blocked by j1w3 + vu32.
  ec7r  Tier 2: conditional effects (type gates, crit gates, crafter choice). Blocked by vqjp.
  bstt  Item activation as a granted action. Independent of the others; wider than runes.
  14ie  The original enrichment-sidecar ticket, now the delivery mechanism for vqjp/ec7r.

Suggested order: vu32 and j1w3 in parallel, then vqjp, then ec7r. bstt any time.

Survey date 2026-08-15, against 141 distinct property runes and 5433 creature gear entries.

title: Rune effects must use the template engine's target+operation vocabulary
description:
Rune effects ship as {operation, subject, value|modifier} with NO target. The consumer that executes effects — pfsrd2-data-api's template engine — decodes Effect{Target, Operation, ...}, has no subject field, calls resolvePath(statBlock, eff.Target) and errors when it cannot resolve. It also has no 'set' operation. So rune effects are not executable by the only engine that exists for this dataset.

I chose 'subject' deliberately, reasoning that JSONPath targets were speculative because no canonical composed item+rune document exists. That reasoning does not survive contact with the consumer: the engine's whole model is target+operation against a stat_block document, an item IS such a document, and applyAddModifier even creates the target array when it is missing.

Nothing is broken today — the only apply endpoint is creature-only — so this is latent. But a second effect vocabulary is exactly the accidental complexity to remove before anything is built on it.

Scope: 13 files, 60 effect objects (the fundamental and reinforcing grades). Materials and spell slots carry no effects at all.
design:
Map each rune effect onto an operation the engine already implements:
  weapon potency -> add_modifier @ $.stat_block.offense.weapon_modes[*].modifiers
  armor potency  -> add_modifier @ $.stat_block.defense.modifiers
  resilient      -> add_modifier @ $.stat_block.defense.modifiers
  striking       -> replace @ $.stat_block.offense.weapon_modes[*].damage[*].dice_count
  reinforcing    -> adjustment @ $.stat_block.defense.hitpoints.{hardness,hp,break_threshold}

adjustment adds a delta and syncs the sibling display text, which is exactly the reinforcing wording. replace sets a value and syncs text. Shields already expose defense.hitpoints.{hardness,hp,break_threshold} so those targets resolve today.

Striking needs dice_count, which weapon damage does not currently expose (only formula: '1d8'). Structuring that is a prerequisite and is worth doing on its own merits per the project mission.

property_rune_slots is capacity metadata rather than a mutation and moves out of effects onto the rune block as grants_property_slots.
acceptance_criteria: No rune effect carries 'subject'; every effect has a target that resolves against at least one real host item, enforced by pf2_verify_runes; operations are drawn only from the engine's vocabulary; weapon damage exposes dice_count and die_size; equipment parser 0 errors.
close_reason: Fixed. Rune effects now use target + operations the template engine implements (add_modifier / replace / adjustment); no effect carries subject. Weapon damage gained dice_count and die_size so striking's target resolves. Capacity moved to rune.grants_property_slots since it mutates nothing. pf2_verify_runes checks every effect target resolves, mutation-verified. Full equipment run 0 errors, all four verifiers green.

title: Staff spell lists silently dropped for 24 of 90 staves
description:
24 of 90 staves parse with variants: [] and no spell list at all, while their source HTML plainly carries one.

Verified cases:
  - Staff of Illumination (aonid 3043): HTML lists 'Cantrip light / 2nd everlight / 3rd everlight, holy light'; JSON has no variants, no rank list, no spell links.
  - Hell Staff (aonid 2253): HTML lists 9 entries across Cantrip-4th (divine lance, protection, summon lesser servitor, darkvision, chilling darkness, divine wrath); JSON has empty variants and only an incidental spell link from flavour text.

The 66 staves that DO parse present their list as markdown bullets inside variant text ('* Cantrip tanglefoot', '* 1st shocking grasp, spider sting'), with higher grades adding ranks cumulatively. The 24 that fail present it inside an 'Activate [action] Cast a Spell; Effect' block with rank-labelled lines and no variant structure — a second layout the parser does not handle.

This is the same class as the legacy Dragonhide stat-table loss fixed in PR #152: content published by AoN, absent from output, with nothing failing. Full list of affected aonids obtainable by re-running the survey in the issue notes.

Fix before any spell-slot decoration work, since that work would otherwise be built on a corpus missing a quarter of its staff spell lists.
design: Two candidate approaches: (a) teach the staff path to read the Activate/Cast-a-Spell effect block as a spell list when no variant bullets exist, or (b) find why these items produce no variants at all — empty variants plus a populated HTML block suggests the variant splitter bails before reaching the effect block. Investigate (b) first; the missing variants may be the actual root cause and the spell list a downstream symptom.
acceptance_criteria: All 90 staves expose their published spell list; a staff whose HTML advertises a Cast-a-Spell rank list but yields none fails the parse rather than shipping empty.
close_reason: Invalid — my survey was wrong. I searched only stat_block.text and variants[].text; staves without grade variants carry their spell list in stat_block.statistics.abilities[].effect, with spell links attached. Verified across the whole document: 88 of 90 staves have a structured rank list, Whispering Staff correctly has none (it functions as a major staff of the unblinking eye, delegating to another item), and Staff of the Black Desert has its list as an undelimited run-on string rather than bullets. No spell content is lost. The run-on formatting variance is real but minor and is folded into the spell-slot work instead.

title: Move creature_types list to enrichment DB table, populated by creature parser
description:
Replace hardcoded _CREATURE_TYPES set in enrichment/change_extractor.py with a DB-backed lookup. The current set is incomplete (misses Vampire, Skeleton, ancestries, elements, Unholy, Aquatic, etc.) which caused the trait-routing fix from a10f0f4 to drop real creature_types entries to $.traits-only.

Design:
1. New creature_types table in enrichment DB (name UNIQUE).
2. Seed script reads existing pfsrd2-data/monsters to populate.
3. Creature parser adds pass to upsert creature_types it encounters (idempotent).
4. _trait_target in change_extractor.py queries DB (cached per-run).
5. Bump ENRICHMENT_VERSION.
close_reason: Enrichment DB creature_types table added (v6 migration). Creature parser runs creature_type_db_pass to upsert types seen. Seed script bin/pf2_seed_creature_types scans pfsrd2-data/monsters+npcs (seeded 221 names). _trait_target now queries DB with per-process cache and reset_creature_types_cache() for tests. title: Fix template 'abilities' change effects: route per-ability instead of all→defense.automatic_abilities
description: _build_effects in enrichment/change_extractor.py hardcodes a single effect targeting $.defense.automatic_abilities for category='abilities'. This causes offensive abilities added by templates (e.g., Amphibious → Drag Along, a one-action offensive ability) to be placed under defense.automatic_abilities alongside genuinely automatic abilities like Low-light Vision. Fix: emit one effect per ability, using each ability's deterministic action-type-based category (reaction→reactive, 1-2-3 action→offensive, free+trigger→reactive) with DB lookup fallback via ability_placement.lookup_ability_category, and filter source JSONPath by ability name.
close_reason: Per-ability effect routing implemented in _build_ability_effects. Amphibious now correctly routes Low-light Vision → senses.special_senses and Drag Along → offense.offensive_actions. 1118 tests pass; full monster_templates and monster_families runs clean.

This will break creature parsing and the ability enrichment DB population (which uses special_sense subtype detection). title: Cache LLM responses to survive enrichment DB rebuilds
description: When the enrichment DB is deleted and rebuilt, all LLM enrichment work is lost and must be re-run (~75 min for damage alone). Design: add an llm_response_cache table keyed on (identity_hash, prompt_version) that stores the raw LLM response. When enriching, check the cache first — if the hash and prompt version match, use the cached response instead of calling the LLM. This table should either: (a) live in a separate DB file that doesn't get deleted, or (b) be resilient to the main enrichment DB being rebuilt by auto-populating from the cache on first access. The cache makes it safe to delete enrichment.db without losing expensive LLM work.

title: Monster family sections tree should remain unmodified by consolidation
description: The _consolidate_creation_changes function removes ability sections from the sections tree when moving them to subtypes. This means the raw sections tree no longer represents the original document structure. For rendering, we need the sections tree to be a faithful representation of the original HTML — changes/subtypes are enrichment overlays, not replacements for sections. Fix: stop removing sections from the tree during consolidation. The subtypes can reference sections by name or path instead of consuming them.
close_reason:
Already fixed — verified against shipped data rather than closed on the code comment alone. The ticket asked for _consolidate_creation_changes to stop removing ability sections from the sections tree, so subtypes become enrichment overlays rather than replacements. monster_family.py now says exactly that at the consolidation site ("Sections are NOT removed — they stay intact for display") and builds each subtype with a JSONPath reference to the section instead of consuming it. VERIFIED IN OUTPUT, not just in code: 632 family files, 153 of them carry subtypes. 153 of 153 subtype names are still present in their file's sections tree. The single apparent miss was dragon_time's 'Young Time Dragon"'. That is not a consolidation failure — the section is present under exactly that name, stray double-quote and all. The quote comes from the source heading

Young Time Dragon"

, and is fixed in pfsrd2-web 5ff060dd3f. Separately pinned by tests/test_ability_continuations.py::TestMonsterFamilyKeepsItsSectionText, added in PR #169: it drives _extract_section_abilities over the shape the ability parser leaves unclaimed and fails if monster_family ever reassigns or consumes section["text"] again. Adding `section["text"] = ""` to that function fails it. Closed rather than left open because the fix predates this session and the ticket's own acceptance is met; the test now guards against regression.

title: Recall Knowledge section missing from creature output

So this stays open and unstarted by choice, not by oversight.

WHEN IT IS PICKED UP, the first step is confirmation rather than a fix: check a
Recall Knowledge section in the source HTML against the same creature's shipped
JSON, and establish that it is absent from output rather than merely moved. Only
then bisect the three causes. Doing it the other way round risks the mistake made
twice elsewhere tonight — attributing a data difference to a branch when
pfsrd2-data was simply behind its own parser.

title: Wire template/family abilities into ability enrichment DB

This means the ability_enrichment_pass needs to walk template/family abilities in addition to creature abilities. For abilities not found in any creature, the enrichment DB becomes the only source of category/placement info — so we need an 'ability_type' field on the ability_records table or a way to flag template-origin abilities.

title: Monster family subtypes: parse ability sub-fields instead of splitting on every <b> tag
description: _parse_ability_nodes in monster_template.py splits on every tag, creating a new ability for each. But some tags are sub-fields of the preceding ability (Trigger, Effect, Requirements, Frequency, Cost, Duration, Critical Success, Success, Failure, Critical Failure). Example from Vampire Basic Abilities: Drink Blood [one-action] Requirements ... Effect ... Currently parsed as 3 separate abilities: "Drink Blood", "Requirements", "Effect" Should be 1 ability "Drink Blood" with requirement and effect fields. Additionally, items like "Immunities", "Climb Speed", "Resistances", "Vampire Weaknesses" are being parsed as abilities but are actually stat modifications that should become changes with appropriate change_category and effects. The creature parser's process_interaction_ability (creatures.py:1331) already handles this correctly — it recognizes addon field names and attaches them to the preceding ability. The fix should apply the same logic to _parse_ability_nodes. Known addon fields (from creatures.py): - Frequency, Trigger, Effect, Duration, Requirement, Requirements - Critical Success, Success, Failure, Critical Failure, Cost Known stat modification labels (should become changes, not abilities): - Immunities, Resistances, Weaknesses (→ immunities/resistances/weaknesses changes) - Climb Speed, Fly Speed, Swim Speed (→ speed changes) - Darkvision, Low-Light Vision (→ senses changes) - Negative/Void Healing (→ actual ability, keep as ability) This affects both monster_template.py and monster_family.py since they share _parse_ability_nodes.

title: Rework activate: activations array vs polymorphic ability extension
description:
The activate pattern is becoming sticky and a poor fit for ability - like affliction, it's a superset of ability rather than fitting cleanly into it.

Two approaches to consider:

1. **Activations array approach**: Create an `activations` array containing `activate` objects. Each activate object can hold an `ability` plus have the `activation` field on it. This separates concerns cleanly.

2. **Polymorphic extension approach**: If JSON Schema supports any kind of polymorphism (oneOf, allOf, discriminator patterns), consider extending the `ability` object to become an `activation` object - essentially making activation a specialized subtype of ability.

Research needed:
- Review JSON Schema polymorphism options (oneOf with discriminator, allOf for inheritance-like patterns)
- Examine how affliction currently handles being a superset of ability
- Determine which approach better fits the existing schema patterns and parser architecture

This affects equipment.py parsing and pfsrd2/schema/equipment.schema.json.
close_reason: Activation type implementation complete. Created separate 'activation' subtype with structured activation_types array, consistent 'Activate' name with optional activation_name field, proper cruft cleanup, and modular price parsing.

Goal: Make the code fail fast and loudly when invariants are violated instead of hiding bugs with defensive checks.

Categories:
- Critical (P0): 3 issues - Type checks, config hiding, default params

- Medium (P2): 6 issues - Try-except, complex conditionals

Testing protocol for each fix:
1. Apply fix
2. Run full test suite on weapons, armor, shields, siege_weapons
3. Document what breaks (if anything)
4. Determine if breakage reveals real bugs or is acceptable

Related PR: #12 (shields support and equipment parsing unification)
