title: Load all actions (skill + general) into the DB so skill_check can reference one
description:
pfsrd2-data has no actions/ directory and PFSRD2-Parser/bin has no pf2_run_actions.sh. The Actions content type is listed in CLAUDE.md but has never been parsed.

This surfaced while validating LLM enrichment caches. Ability text routinely names an Escape DC:

  'The DC to Escape or Force Open the web is 30'          Web Tether
  'Any creature hit by the puppeteer's string is grabbed'  Clockwork String
  'attempts to pull a Medium or smaller creature it has grabbed'  Encase
  'the grabbed creature can attempt to Escape as normal, but the DC to do so is 40'  Impaling Charge

Escape is NOT a skill action. It is game-obj 'Actions', aonid 79 — it can be attempted with Acrobatics, Athletics, or an unarmed attack modifier, so it does not live under any one skill. The skills corpus references it only as a link:

  {"alt": "Escape", "aonid": 79, "game-obj": "Actions", "name": "Escape", "type": "link"}

Force Open, Grapple, Climb and the other 73 skill actions DO exist, published as skill.actions[] with subtype 'skill_action'. So half of the action DCs in creature text can be resolved today and half cannot.

Scope: parse the Actions pages from pfsrd2-web into pfsrd2-data/actions/, following the existing skill_action shape (name, action_type, traits, links, degrees of success).

Relationship to 2cby: 2cby introduces the skill_check object type. It should carry a game-obj/aonid pair so it can point at either corpus; this ticket makes the Actions half resolvable. 2cby can land first and simply leave Escape unresolved.
design:
DESIGN DIRECTION (Devon, 2026-08-21): the target is ALL actions of BOTH types
in the pfsrd2 database, so a skill_check (PFSRD2-Parser-2cby) can carry an
optional action reference.

That widens this ticket beyond "parse the Actions pages". Two sources feed one
table:

1. General actions -- the Actions corpus, never parsed. No actions/ directory
   in pfsrd2-data, no bin/pf2_run_actions.sh. Escape is game-obj "Actions",
   aonid 79. This is the new-parser half.

2. Skill actions -- ALREADY parsed, but only as nested structure. All 73 live
   inside skills/*/*.json under skill.actions[] with subtype "skill_action".
   They carry name, action_type, traits, sample_tasks, links, and the degrees
   of success -- but no game_id, so nothing can reference them. This half is
   an extraction/loader job, not a parsing job: the data is already correct,
   it just is not addressable.

Both land in one actions table following pfsrd2/sql/traits.py and
monster_abilities.py: game_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, create/truncate/insert,
and a fetch_action_by_name for parse-time resolution the way trait_db_pass
works. One table, because skill_check should not care which corpus an action
came from -- "Escape" and "Force Open" appear side by side in the same
sentence ("The DC to Escape or Force Open the web is 30") and must resolve the
same way.

Uniqueness is the part to get right up front (see game-id-is-a-unique-id):
  - Escape is linked from both acrobatics and athletics -> ONE row.
  - Force Open, Grapple, Climb etc. are republished in core_rulebook AND
    player_core -> ONE row per action, with edition handled the way the rest
    of the pipeline handles it, not one row per book.

Sequencing: 2cby defines the skill_check shape and can land first with the
action reference left unresolved. This ticket makes both halves resolvable.

ADDED 2026-08-21 -- the actions table must carry a skills field.

PFSRD2-Parser-2cby settled on the check NOT storing skills: it hangs a dc and
an action, and the permitted skills are derived by following the action. That
makes this table the single source of truth for which skills an action allows,
so 'skills' is a required part of the row, not a nice-to-have.

Populating it differs by half:

  skill actions    implied by the parent page. Force Open is on the Athletics
                   page -> [Athletics]. But Escape is linked from BOTH
                   acrobatics and athletics, so the implication is not always
                   single-valued -- do not assume one skill per action.

  general actions  stated in the action's own prose, e.g. Escape
                   (Actions.aspx.ID_79): 'typically the Athletics DC... the
                   Thievery DC... You can attempt an Acrobatics check instead'.

DECIDE BEFORE BUILDING: Escape also permits 'your unarmed attack modifier',
which is not a skill at all. A plain array of skill names stores Escape
lossily. Either model non-skill modifiers in the same field or accept the loss
knowingly -- Escape is the most common action named in creature ability text,
so this choice is load-bearing rather than academic.
acceptance_criteria:
pfsrd2-data/actions/ exists, populated from the 615 parse-ready pages in pfsrd2-web/2e.aonprd.com/Actions/.

The 73 skill actions currently nested in skills/*/*.json under skill.actions[] are addressable as first-class objects with a game_id, not only as nested structure.

Both kinds live in one actions table (pattern: pfsrd2/sql/traits.py) keyed on game_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, with a fetch_action_by_name for parse-time resolution.

Each action carries its permitted skills, able to hold MORE THAN ONE, and able to represent Escape's non-skill 'unarmed attack modifier' without loss.

Escape resolves to exactly one row despite being linked from both acrobatics and athletics. Force Open, Grapple, Climb etc. resolve to one row each despite being republished in both core_rulebook and player_core.

A decision is recorded (either way) on whether the 24 item-activation pages become action objects here or stay owned by the item under PFSRD2-Parser-bstt.
notes:
SURVEYED THE WEB CORPUS 2026-08-21 -- this is a full parser, not a small job.

pfsrd2-web/2e.aonprd.com/Actions/ exists and holds 639 pages.

  615  parse-ready: a real h1 carrying name and action cost
   24  no usable h1 -- see below, they are item activations

Action cost markers on the 615:

    214  [one-action]
    179  (none)            <- activities and exploration/downtime actions
    110  [two-actions]
     71  [reaction]
     31  [free-action]
     10  [three-actions]

Structure present:

    223  degrees of success (critical success / success / failure / ...)
    196  Requirements
     86  Trigger

So the shape is close to the skill_action already parsed out of skills/*.json
(name, action_type, traits, source, text, degrees) -- the existing
skill_action structure is the model to follow, which is what makes one shared
actions table realistic.

THE 24 WITHOUT AN H1 ARE ITEM ACTIVATIONS, not a parse failure:

    Actions.aspx.ID_138   "Activate [one-action] Climb; Requirements You are
                           trained in Athletics..."
    Actions.aspx.ID_2336  "Activate —Set Free [two-actions] (concentrate,
                           manipulate); Effect..."
    Actions.aspx.ID_2229  "Activate [reaction] manipulate; Trigger The shield
                           is broken..."

These are the action an item grants, so they overlap PFSRD2-Parser-bstt (Item
activation: an activatable item grants an action). Decide deliberately whether
they become action objects here, or belong to the item and are skipped by this
parser. Do not let them fall between the two tickets.

Two more things the parser must handle, found in the same survey:

  - Decorative h1s. Every page carries "Classic Feel", "Book Feel", "Round
    Feel", "Slim Feel" as h1 elements (display-style variants) plus "Archives
    of Nethys" and "Actions | Activities". These must be filtered or the name
    extraction picks up a stylesheet toggle.

  - The documented HTML5 shape applies: content lives under cssclass="main"
    (id="main"), with nav before the first <hr>. Reuse the _content_filter
    pattern rather than reinventing it.

TWO CONSTRAINTS ADDED (Devon, 2026-08-21), both verified against the data.

1. RESOLVE FROM THE LINK ALREADY ON THE OBJECT, NOT FROM THE PROSE.

In most cases the object already carries a link pointing at the right skill or
action -- but keyed by aonid, not game-id. href_filter has already done the
work. MEASURED over the 31 misfiled DCs in the enrichment cache:

    12  carries an Actions link
     8  carries BOTH an Actions and a Skills link
     1  carries a Skills link
    10  carries neither

  21 of 31 are resolvable without reading the prose at all:

    Impaling Charge  {"alt": "Escape", "aonid": 79, "game-obj": "Actions", ...}
    Whiffling        {"alt": "Acrobatics", "aonid": 1, "game-obj": "Skills", ...}
                     {"alt": "Maneuver in Flight", "aonid": 30, "game-obj": "Actions", ...}
    Modular Arms     {"alt": "Thievery", "aonid": 17, "game-obj": "Skills", ...}
                     {"alt": "Disable a Device", "aonid": 69, "game-obj": "Actions", ...}

So the classifier is primarily a LINK reader, and text matching is the
fallback for the ~10 that carry no link. This is both more reliable than
matching names in prose and independently confirms the action_check refinement:
the 8 "both" cases literally carry both links, which is exactly the
"DC N <Skill> check to <Action>" shape.

Note the join is aonid -> game_id. The actions table is keyed on game_id
(unique), so it needs an aonid lookup path as well, or the link cannot be
followed. Do not resolve by name where an aonid is present -- names collide
across editions and corpora, aonids do not.

2. EDITION MUST PAIR: legacy to legacy, remastered to remastered.

Same rule as everywhere else in this codebase. The precedent to copy is
trait_db_pass._handle_trait_link in pfsrd2/sql/traits.py: compare the fetched
row's edition against struct["edition"], and where they differ, follow
alternate_link to the matching-edition twin and assert loudly if that twin is
missing. There is also fetch_trait_by_name_preferring_edition, written because
"nearly every trait exists as both legacy and remastered rows; without an
ORDER BY the row returned is arbitrary, which makes embedded game-id/sources
nondeterministic". Actions have exactly that problem -- Force Open, Grapple and
Climb are published in both core_rulebook and player_core -- so the actions
table needs the same edition-preferring fetch, not a bare name lookup.

A remastered creature must not end up pointing at a legacy Escape.

VALIDATE THE LINKAGE (Devon, 2026-08-21). Links are sometimes missing, and
sometimes point at the wrong object. Traits already validate this; skills and
actions must do the same going forward.

The precedent is pfsrd2/sql/traits.py trait_db_pass:

    data = fetch_trait_by_name(curs, trait["name"])
    assert data, f"Trait not found in database: {trait}"
    ...
    assert data, f"Trait has alternate_link but linked trait not found in DB: ..."

i.e. resolve, and fail loudly when resolution fails, rather than emitting an
unresolved or half-resolved object.

MEASURED -- every Skills link on every ability record, checked by asking
whether the link's aonid actually points at the skill the link names.
1160 links total:

   1088  exact match
     67  Lore specialisation -- LEGITIMATE, must not fail
      3  case / alias only   -- normalise, do not fail
      2  WRONG OBJECT        -- genuinely broken source data

The two categories that matter:

  LEGITIMATE, and a naive validator would reject all 67:
      "Sailing Lore" -> aonid 8, which is the Lore skill.
    AoN points every Lore variant at the single Lore page, so the link name is
    a specialisation of the target's name rather than equal to it. Validation
    must allow "<X> Lore" -> Lore. Also allow case differences ("deception" ->
    Deception) and the known alias "Intimidate" -> Intimidation.

  GENUINELY BROKEN, and this is what validation is FOR:
      Weakening Strike carries {"name": "enfeebled 1", "game-obj": "Skills",
      "aonid": 13} and {"name": "enfeebled 2", ...}. enfeebled is a CONDITION,
      not a skill, and aonid 13 is Religion. Trusting game-obj here files a
      condition as a skill with a wholly unrelated aonid.

So the rule is: resolve the link, compare the resolved object's name against
the link's name under a normalisation that permits Lore specialisation, case,
and known aliases -- and fail loudly on anything left over. Do NOT silently
fall back to name-matching the prose when the link disagrees; that hides the
broken source data instead of surfacing it, which is the same mistake as
filing these DCs under saving_throw in the first place.

MISSING links are the other half: 10 of the 31 misfiled DCs carry no
Skills/Actions link at all. Those fall back to reading the prose, and are the
cases most likely to stay unclassifiable. That is expected, not a defect.

This also bounds how far the LLM should be trusted with link context (see the
note above): the links are good evidence, not ground truth, so a save/skill
classification that contradicts a validated link should surface rather than
silently pick one.

title: Use ollama constrained decoding (JSON schema + regex) for LLM extraction
description:
Ollama 0.32.5 on valid.evilsoft supports constrained decoding: pass a JSON
Schema as "format" and the model can only emit conforming output. Measured on
an 11-case bench built from known-bad extractions (the ntsj set plus the l59s
deferred-DC case), this beats every model swap that was tried.

RESULTS, qwen2.5:7b throughout, scored as "does the answer CONTAIN the values
the source states":

  free text, current pipeline    baseline (5/11 exact; see model table below)
  structured, schema only        6/11 contains
  structured + regex on formula  9/11 contains, 8s for 11 cases

The regex is what does the work. A bare schema constrains SHAPE, so the model
still wrote prose into the formula field -- "3d6 bludgeoning damage",
"longsword damage" -- and leaked unrelated integers such as "36" out of
"Rupture 36". Adding

    "formula": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9]+d[0-9]+([+-][0-9]+)?$"}

removed that entire class. Cases that are WRONG in shipped data today and come
out right under this: Sapping Squeeze (exact), Shell Rake, Breath Weapon,
Stampede, Focused Assault, Focused Flames.

MODEL COMPARISON on the same bench, free-text prompt, exact match:

    qwen2.5:7b     5/11    cached
    gemma4:26b     4/11    152s
    gemma3n:e4b    4/11     20s
    qwen3:8b       4/11    217s
    qwen3.5:9b     2/11   1065s

Nothing beat qwen2.5:7b, and the newer reasoning models were both slower and
worse -- they over-reason a task that wants literal extraction. qwen2.5:14b and
:32b are being pulled to test the "scale the family that already adheres"
axis. The 35b on the box is a coding model and was not worth finishing.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX. Two bench cases miss under every configuration, and
they are the same class: damage that belongs to a DIFFERENT ability in the same
text. Pack Attack takes Swallow Whole's 3d12+10; Dragon's Wisdom takes an
unrelated 21d6. No schema fixes attribution. That is a prompt problem and
possibly a text-segmentation problem upstream, and it is what remains of ntsj
after the stale-prompt correction.

ALSO NEEDED: dedup. The structured run emitted 3d10 four times for Generate
Bomb. Harmless but it must not reach the data.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES

  * Schemas belong in llm_config.toml beside the prompts, for the same reason
    the prompts moved there: they are tuning, not logic.
  * llm_cache keys on a hash of the rendered prompt. A structured request is a
    different request, so cached free-text answers do not collide -- but the
    cache key should include the schema, or a schema change will silently
    return a stale answer shaped by the old one.
  * The response parser (_clean_llm_response / _parse_damage_response) becomes
    largely unnecessary for any extractor that moves to structured output. Do
    not delete it until every extractor has moved; frequency, area, dc and
    category all still use the free-text path.
  * Keep the grounding guard regardless. Constrained decoding stops malformed
    output, not invented numbers -- a schema-valid 9d9 is still a fabrication.

CAVEAT ON THE EVIDENCE: 11 cases, every one drawn from a known failure. This is
a strong signal about the failure classes it covers and NOT a corpus-wide
accuracy figure. Before switching the pipeline over, re-measure on a random
sample that includes cases the current pipeline gets right, to confirm no
regression.
notes:
Constrained decoding is in and validated against all 1580 cached LLM values (damage, saving_throw, area, frequency): 527 -> 154 disagreements.

Key finding, recorded in memory as filter-dont-instruct: constrained decoding makes fabrication EASIER, not harder. The schema pattern guarantees output looks valid, so bare numbers get completed into plausible values ('30-foot cone' -> 30d6, '3 rounds in total' -> 3d12, '+2 circumstance bonus' -> 2d6+6). Four mechanical grounding filters now backstop it: _dcs_in, _save_types_in, _dice_in, _area_sizes_in.

Four prompt revisions were measured and all were worse than baseline; see the comment above the damage prompt in llm_config.toml. Do not retune that prompt.

Commits: 82f5d2e, 390f411, bae1d46, 29beaaf on fix/ollama-host.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
UPDATE: prototype landed on fix/ollama-host (c1418d5), and the 14b result is in.

qwen2.5:14b under structured decoding scores IDENTICALLY to 7b -- 10/11
containing, 13s vs 10s. Scaling the family does not help. The decoding
constraint is the entire win, and 7b stays the model.

Final bench, structured + regex, both models:

    qwen2.5:7b    exact 3/11   contains 10/11   10s
    qwen2.5:14b   exact 3/11   contains 10/11   13s

The single remaining miss on both is Pack Attack, which is the attribution
problem: "The nornhound's Strikes deal 1d6 extra damage ... Swallow Whole
(attack); Huge, 3d12+10 bludgeoning" -- two abilities in one blob of text, and
the model takes the wrong one's damage. 7b returned 3d12+10; 14b returned
nothing at all. Neither is right, and no schema fixes it.

Worth noting the pattern is not airtight either: 7b emitted "36d6" once,
assembled out of "Rupture 36". It is well-formed dice, so the regex admits it.
The grounding guard catches it (36d6 does not occur in the text), which is the
argument for keeping both layers.

WHAT WAS SEARCHED, on the "is anything beating qwen2.5 for this" question:

  NuExtract (numind) -- models fine-tuned specifically for text-to-JSON
  extraction, which is exactly this task. NuExtract-2.0-8B is built on
  Qwen2.5-VL; there is an ollama build of the tiny variant
  (sroecker/nuextract-tiny-v1.5). This is the most promising untried option and
  is worth a bench run.

  GLiNER2 -- schema-driven IE, encoder-based, very fast. Built for entities and
  relations rather than dice formulae, so probably a poor fit here, but cheap
  to disprove.

  Reported consensus matches what was measured locally: the Qwen2.5 family is
  strong at schema adherence, and below roughly 4B parameters extraction
  accuracy is dominated by compliance failures rather than reading errors --
  which is why the 0.5b and 3b variants on the box were not worth testing.

NEXT STEPS, in order of value:

  1. Re-measure on a RANDOM sample that includes cases the current pipeline
     gets right. The 11-case bench is deliberately adversarial and says nothing
     about regression risk.
  2. Bench NuExtract against the same cases.
  3. Move the remaining four extractors (frequency, area, dc, category) once
     damage is proven on a random sample.
  4. Attribution is a separate problem and probably belongs upstream: the
     Pack Attack text contains two abilities because the parser handed the
     enricher a blob that spans both.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
NuExtract tried and rejected. Also: a temperature finding that matters more.

NUEXTRACT-TINY (sroecker/nuextract-tiny-v1.5, a 0.5B Qwen2.5 fine-tune -- the
only NuExtract build in the ollama registry):

    exact 0/11, contains 0/11.

Tested fairly, after two false starts that were my error rather than the
model's:

  1. Its native format is "<|input|>\n### Template:\n{tmpl}\n### Text:\n{text}
     \n\n<|output|>", and ollama's packaging wraps prompts in a Qwen chat
     template that injected "You are a helpful assistant." into the output.
     Fixed with "raw": true.
  2. With a nested template ({"damage": [{"formula": "", "damage_type": ""}]})
     it returns empty or nothing at all.

Given a FLAT template it does extract -- but the wrong thing:

    template {"damage": []}
    text     "...dealing 1d6+5 bludgeoning and 1d4 persistent bleed damage..."
    output   {"damage": ["bludgeoning", "persistent bleed"]}

It pulled the damage TYPES and dropped the dice. That is a 0.5B model behaving
exactly as the literature predicts below ~4B, where compliance failures
dominate over reading.

The NuExtract variants that would be worth testing are v1.5 (3.8B, Phi-3.5-mini)
and v2.0-8B (Qwen2.5-VL). Neither is in the ollama registry under any obvious
name -- all four candidates 404. Using them means converting from HuggingFace
weights, which is a bigger job than this is worth while qwen2.5:7b with
constrained decoding already reaches 10/11.

THE TEMPERATURE FINDING, which is independent of NuExtract and applies to the
pipeline today:

NuExtract's model card notes that extraction wants temperature at or near 0,
and that ollama's default of 0.7 is actively bad for it. Our pipeline sets NO
options, so every extraction ever made has run at 0.7.

    qwen2.5:7b, structured, default 0.7   exact 3/11, contains 10/11
    qwen2.5:7b, structured, temperature 0 exact 4/11, contains 10/11

The exact-match improvement is small and the containment is unchanged, so this
is not a quality breakthrough. The reason to do it anyway is DETERMINISM: at
0.7 the same prompt returns different answers on different runs, which means
the llm_cache is memoising a coin flip, a re-enrichment silently changes data
that nobody edited, and no regression test over this pipeline can be trusted.

RECOMMENDATION: set temperature 0 in llm_config.toml for all extractors. It is
a two-line change and it makes every other measurement in this ticket
reproducible.

title: HTML: doubled <b> swallows the ability name in Dwarf Longshot Squad (name absent from source)
description:
ability_id 10622 and 17448 in the enrichment DB are named 'Frequency once per round'. A Frequency line has been consumed as the ability name. Both are dwarven longshot troop abilities whose real name is missing.

Found while hand-validating LLM enrichment picks for PR #175; unrelated to enrichment, this is a parse defect in the ability name extraction.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text: CORRECTED: this is an HTML bug, not a parse bug. I filed it against the parser and the maintainer called it correctly. The source HTML at Monsters.aspx.ID_3914 (Dwarf Longshot Squad) reads: Frequency once per round Effect Using blades attached to their crossbows... The label is wrapped twice, so the OUTER bold -- which is where an ability name belongs -- contains "Frequency once per round" instead. 167 troop and NPC abilities in this corpus use the well-formed shape, Name ... Frequency value, so the parser is reading correct markup correctly and this markup is wrong. There is a second defect in the same block: a stray empty inside the three-action damage line, which is why one of the two records has text starting " piercing damage". WHY THIS ONE IS NOT FIXED YET. The ability's name is absent from the HTML altogether. There is no preceding span holding it, unlike the sibling case at NPCs.aspx.ID_2544 where the name (Defensive Charm) was present and merely split off by a premature -- that one is fixed in PFSRD2-Web PR #5. The other abilities on this creature are Bolts from the Blue, Hampering Fusillade and Longshots With Guns; the missing one is the melee troop attack with the one/two/three-action damage ladder (1d8+2 / 2d8+11 / 3d8+13 piercing). Its name has to come from Battlecry or the live AoN page. It cannot be inferred from the file. Shipped consequence today: monsters/battlecry/dwarf_longshot_squad.json carries an ability named "Frequency once per round". A third apparent instance, monsters/.../the_guest.json with "Trigger Memory", is a FALSE POSITIVE -- that is a genuine ability name and the markup is fine.

title: Regex extractor cannot read compound damage types ('7d6 fire and bludgeoning damage')
description:
pfsrd2/enrichment/regex_extractor.extract_all handles a single damage type but not two joined by "and" or "or":

  "dealing 7d6 fire damage to all creatures"                 -> 7d6 fire
  "dealing 7d6 fire and bludgeoning damage to all creatures" -> nothing, reported in missed
  "dealing 7d6 fire or bludgeoning damage to all creatures"  -> nothing, reported in missed

This is honest under-extraction rather than silent: the keyword lands in the "missed" dict, so the record is flagged and the LLM pass picks it up. But it means the value is only ever available via the LLM, which is expensive and — as PFSRD2-Parser-l59s showed — sometimes fabricates.

Live instance, found while auditing PR #175's data changes:

  npcs/npc_core/rocketeer.json, ability "Explosive Liftoff" (ability_id 14494)
  effect: "...dealing 7d6 fire and bludgeoning damage to all creatures in a
           15-foot emanation with a DC 24 basic Reflex save."

Published damage went from 7d6 to absent. The cached LLM value was superseded by a fresh LLM call that returned a fabricated 1d6, which the grounding guard correctly rejected — leaving no value at all, because the regex cannot derive the real one. The record is needs_review with an "--llm-type damage" reason and will be retried.

Fixing this in the regex removes an LLM dependency for a whole sentence shape and is worth more than one file. Measure how many corpus abilities match the compound pattern before sizing it.

title: Spells with two saves model only the first: Depart/second-effect degrees are absent (tempest_of_shades)
description:
spells/secrets_of_magic/tempest_of_shades.json models only its FIRST save. The spell has two, and the second's degrees of success are absent from the data entirely.

The spell prints an Arrive effect with a Fortitude save and its four degrees, then a **Depart** effect -- *Howl of Eternity* -- with its own Will save and its own degrees. The file carries a single `defense` object holding the Arrive degrees, and the spell `text` ends at "...must attempt a Fortitude save with the following effects." The Depart block is not represented at all.

Found while reviewing the degree-boundary work on PR #175. Not caused by it: HEAD has the same gap and "Howl of Eternity" has never appeared in any commit of this file.

One detail worth recording because it is easy to misread. During the boundary work an intermediate parser build DID capture the Depart paragraph into the spell's `text` (with three trait links: emotion, fear, mental). That build was superseded and the capture is gone again. So a reviewer comparing against a stale index blob will see the text appear and then disappear; neither state modelled the second save's DEGREES, only the prose.

The same shape appears in:

  spells/war_of_immortals/final_fate_of_the_locust_host.json   Depart, own basic Reflex save

and is the underlying reason both files show up under PFSRD2-Parser-xqzp: when a Depart block IS absorbed into the preceding degree, its damage gets attributed to the wrong save. Bounding the degree correctly stops the misattribution but leaves the second save unmodelled, which is this ticket.

WHAT IS NEEDED

The schema's `spell_defense` is a single object. A spell with two saves needs either a list of defenses or a separate object per effect (Arrive / Depart), plus the parser recognising the second block. Deciding the shape is the first step; both files above should be checked together, and a corpus sweep for "**Depart**" in spell text will show whether there are more.

title: degree_effects drops all flat and splash damage: only dice are extracted (378 entries, 0 non-dice)
description:
degree_effects only ever emits DICE. Across the entire monsters + npcs corpus there are 378 damage entries and ZERO non-dice formulas and ZERO splash flags. Every flat damage value in a degree is silently dropped.

The result is misleading rather than merely incomplete: a degree that deals flat damage looks identical to a degree that deals none, and in several cases the WORST outcome is the one that disappears while the lesser ones keep their entries.

  monsters/kingmaker_adventure_path/immense_mandragora.json  Apocalyptic Shriek
      success          8d8   -> captured
      failure         16d8   -> captured
      critical_failure "takes 150 mental damage" -> NOTHING

  npcs/pathfinder_174_.../unshadowed_{anchor_root,haibram,koride,mariama,okoro}.json
      Rupture Shadow
      success          "5 acid splash damage"   -> nothing
      failure          "10 acid splash damage"  -> nothing
      critical_failure "20 acid splash damage" + 4d6 persistent acid
                       -> only the 4d6

  monsters/*/immolis.json (x2)  Heat Beam
      critical_failure "4d6+5 fire damage and 5 persistent fire damage"
                       -> only the 4d6+5

  weatherhazards/kingmaker_companion_guide/tornado.json  routine
      critical_failure "an additional 60 points of bludgeoning damage from the
                       fall" -> nothing, while success (4d6+4d6) and failure
                       (8d6+8d6) are captured

  spells/player_core/massacre.json                 "takes 100 void damage"
  spells/.../song_of_the_fallen.json               "100 positive damage"
  feats/*/lethal_finisher.json (x2)  critical_success "You deal 6 precision damage."

NOT A SCHEMA LIMIT. attack_damage.formula is a free string and the corpus already
contains flat formulas elsewhere -- 50 instances of "1", plus "2", "3", "20".
splash is a declared boolean property. Both are expressible today; the extractor
simply does not produce them from degree text.

WHERE IT LIVES

pfsrd2/enrichment/regex_extractor.py, the damage patterns behind extract_all.
They match dice expressions (NdM, NdM+K); "150 mental damage" and "20 acid splash
damage" match nothing.

WORTH DECIDING AT THE SAME TIME

Whether splash should set splash: true rather than being folded in as ordinary
damage -- the property exists and nothing sets it from a degree, so a consumer
cannot currently tell splash from direct damage anywhere in degree_effects.

Found by per-file review of the creature corpus during PR #175. The affected
files were staged rather than held, because this is a uniform corpus-wide
limitation and not a regression -- holding them would have buried the real
per-file findings. Say so if they should wait for this instead.

title: Spell-inflicted afflictions are prose: route the stage block to the existing affliction parser (21 spells)
description:
When a spell inflicts an affliction, AoN prints the affliction's whole stat block after the degrees of success, separated by a paragraph break: Critical Failure The target is afflicted with purple worm venom at stage 2.

Purple Worm Venom (poison); Level 11; Maximum Duration 6 rounds. Stage 1 3d6 poison damage and enfeebled 2 (1 round); Stage 2 4d6 ... Until PFSRD2-Parser-t132 was fixed, that block was absorbed into the critical failure's text. It is now correctly left on the page and flows into the spell's description -- honest, but unstructured. The spell says "afflicted with purple worm venom at stage 2" and nothing in the data says what that venom DOES. 21 spells carry a folded affliction block. Detect them with: a degree string, or now a spell description, containing "**Stage 1**" alongside "**Maximum Duration**" or "**Level**" spells/core_rulebook/{purple_worm_sting,spider_sting,ghoulish_cravings,goblin_pox}.json spells/player_core/{curse_of_death,spider_sting,goblin_pox}.json spells/advanced_players_guide/curse_of_death.json spells/battlecry/{blinding_bottle,blister_bomb}.json spells/pathfinder_160_.../{leng_sting,linnorm_sting,swarming_wasp_stings,wyvern_sting,imp_sting}.json spells/gatewalkers_hardcover/advanced_scurvy.json spells/pathfinder_188_.../advanced_scurvy.json spells/gods__magic/divine_plagues.json spells/howl_of_the_wild/mycological_malady.json spells/malevolence/internal_insurrection.json spells/pathfinder_203_.../cordyceps_command.json The parser already models standalone afflictions: pfsrd2/affliction.py parses Afflictions/*.html into a structured object with stages, onset, maximum duration and saving throw, and the affliction schema already has the shape. So this is mostly a matter of routing -- recognising the block after the degrees, handing it to the existing affliction code, and attaching the result to the spell rather than leaving it as prose. Worth deciding at the same time: many of these afflictions ALSO exist as their own Afflictions page. If so the spell could carry a link rather than an inlined copy, and the two representations should not be allowed to drift. Check purple worm venom, spider venom and ghoul fever before choosing. Split out of PFSRD2-Parser-t132, which fixed the text absorption but explicitly did not model what was absorbed.

title: degree_effects flattens scaling stated inside the degree, emitting only the base case
description:
A degree states its damage AND how that damage scales, in the same sentence. degree_effects records only the base and silently drops the scaling, so the emitted value is right at exactly one character level and wrong at every other.

  feats/pathfinder_201_pactbreaker/death_from_above.json   critical_success
    "...deals an additional 1d6 bludgeoning damage. This additional damage
     increases to 2d6 if you are a master in Athletics, and to 3d6 if you are
     legendary in Athletics."
    emitted: 1d6 bludgeoning

  feats/tian_xia_character_guide/silk_bracelet.json        failure
    "...the target takes an additional 1d4 persistent poison damage. The poison
     damage increases to 2d4 at 12th level and 3d4 at 18th level."
    emitted: 1d4 persistent poison

  feats/gatewalkers_players_guide_remastered/feed_the_void.json  critical_failure
    "...deals 5d6 spirit damage ... At 12th level, and every 2 levels
     thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6."
    emitted: 5d6 spirit
    (this file is held primarily under PFSRD2-Parser-xqzp; the flattened
     scaling is a second defect in the same degree)

  spells/secrets_of_magic/warriors_regret.json             success
    "...takes 1d8 damage per different creature it intentionally damaged (1d8
     if one, 2d8 if two, and so on). The maximum is 4d8..."
    emitted: 1d8 untyped
    (scaling on a different axis -- number of creatures, not level)

Not the same as PFSRD2-Parser-qhtz. There the degree states dice and NOTHING is
emitted. Here something IS emitted, and it looks authoritative while being
incomplete. A consumer has no way to tell the two apart from the data.

Deliberately excluded, for the record: scaling stated in the ability's general
text rather than inside the degree (feats/.../worms_feast.json,
weatherhazards/.../subsidence.json's Major Subsidence). Those degrees are
captured exactly as written and the scaling text is preserved elsewhere in the
object, so the degree itself is not lying. The line drawn is "scaling inside
the degree text".

Options:
 1. Accept and document: degree_effects is the base case, consumers apply
    scaling from the text. Cheap, but the field then cannot be used alone.
 2. Emit nothing when the degree also states a scaling clause -- fails closed,
    consistent with qhtz's current behaviour, loses a real value.
 3. Model it. degree_effect was deliberately built as an extensible object, so
    a `scaling` key is expressible. Needs a decision on what shape (per-level?
    per-proficiency? per-target-count? all three appear above).

Found by per-file review of the feat and spell data diffs on PR #175.
notes:
DECISION (maintainer, 2026-08-17): for now, scaling damage is treated purely as PROSE.

Concretely, this is option 1 from the description and it is the CURRENT behaviour, now deliberate rather than accidental:

  * The degree's base damage is extracted into degree_effects as it is today.
  * The scaling clause stays in the degree's text and is NOT modelled.
  * degree_effects is therefore the base case only. A consumer that needs the
    scaled value reads the degree text.

Consequence for PR #175's data: a file whose ONLY defect was a flattened scaling
ladder is now correct-as-specified and can be staged. Staged on this decision:

  feats/pathfinder_201_pactbreaker/death_from_above.json    1d6 base, ladder to 2d6/3d6 by Athletics proficiency
  feats/tian_xia_character_guide/silk_bracelet.json         1d4 persistent base, ladder to 2d4/3d4 by level
  spells/secrets_of_magic/warriors_regret.json              1d8 base, scales per creature damaged, max 4d8

Still held, because scaling is NOT their only defect:

  feats/.../feed_the_void.json      held under PFSRD2-Parser-xqzp (a non-degree
                                    paragraph merged into the degree); the
                                    flattened "+1d6 every 2 levels" is secondary
  hazards/kingmaker_adventure_path/test_of_endurance.json
                                    NOT the same shape and deliberately still
                                    held. "takes 1d6 cold damage FOR EACH
                                    revolution the wheel has been rotated (max
                                    7d6)" is a per-unit RATE, not a level
                                    ladder. The emitted 1d6 is not the damage at
                                    any point a character actually experiences
                                    unless exactly one revolution has occurred,
                                    so it reads as a plain understatement rather
                                    than as a documented base case. Wants its
                                    own decision.

What remains open, for whenever this is revisited: the schema description for
degree_effect should say that damage is the base case and that scaling stated in
the degree text is not modelled. Without that line the field silently claims
more than it delivers, which is the same complaint as the "double damage"
incompleteness already recorded on PFSRD2-Parser-qhtz.

title: degree_effects under-extracts stated dice and mis-models alternatives (7 spells)
description:
Two degrees state dice damage plainly and degree_effects (PFSRD2-Parser-e01u) emits nothing, and two more state damage the extractor cannot express.

UNDER-EXTRACTION — dice stated, nothing emitted:

  spells/advanced_players_guide/personal_blizzard.json  critical_failure
     "As failure, but both the cold damage and the persistent cold damage
      increase to 2d6."
  spells/player_core/personal_blizzard.json             critical_failure
     "As failure, but both the cold damage and the persistent cold damage
      are 2d6."
  spells/core_rulebook/spellwrack.json                  critical_failure
     "As failure, but the persistent force damage is 4d12."
  spells/player_core/spellwrack.json                    critical_failure
     same
  spells/secrets_of_magic/bloodspray_curse.json         success
     "...the first time each round that the target takes at least 10 piercing
      or slashing damage ... it takes 2d6 additional damage of the same type."

The first four are "As failure, but X is now N" MODIFIERS. Emitting nothing is defensible — the degree does not deal 2d6, it changes another degree's 2d6 — and the strategic-fragility review of PR #175 explicitly argued against asserting on this shape for exactly that reason. But it sits badly next to PFSRD2-Parser-t132, where the same fold-in-a-degree situation OVER-extracts. The two should be decided together.

bloodspray_curse is different and looks like a real gap: 2d6 is damage that degree's subject takes. The schema already has an "of the same type" damage_type enum value, and untyped damage is emitted elsewhere (cup_of_dust, feast_of_ashes), so there is no expressiveness reason to skip it.

CANNOT BE EXPRESSED — emitted, but wrong or lossy:

  spells/rival_academies/unravel_knowledge.json         failure
     "...they take 3d8 mental damage ... the target takes 3d4 mental damage
      INSTEAD if you choose a basic action..."
     emitted: 3d8 mental AND 3d4 mental, as if cumulative.
     These are mutually exclusive alternatives. This one is simply wrong.

  spells/secrets_of_magic/warriors_regret.json          success
     "...takes 1d8 damage per different creature it intentionally damaged
      (1d8 if one, 2d8 if two, and so on). The maximum is 4d8..."
     emitted: 1d8 untyped.
     A scaling formula flattened to its one-creature case; 2d8/4d8 dropped.

Two related gaps found in the same review that are consistent rather than
per-file, and are NOT filed as defects, only recorded here:

  * Flat, non-dice damage is never extracted at all --- massacre "takes 100
    void damage", song_of_the_fallen "100 positive damage", noxious_metals
    "1 persistent poison damage". Consistent, but a consumer expecting every
    damaging degree to carry an entry will not get one.
  * "double damage" / "half damage" correctly produce no numeric effect, which
    means a critical_success degree_effect is often INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: it
    holds the rider (e.g. 1d4 persistent fire) and not the doubled base. A
    consumer summing degree_effects gets the wrong total. Confirmed across
    fire_ray, produce_flame, ignition, live_wire, slashing_gust, blood_feast,
    murmuration, croak_voice, vibrant_vibrato, ray_of_corruption,
    ignite_fireworks, gasping_marsh and both crushing_ground files.

Found by a per-file review of all 78 changed spell files while staging PR #175's data. The 7 named files are held unstaged.

title: Non-degree paragraphs merged into a spell's last degree, so degree_effects attributes their damage wrongly (6 spells)
description:
A paragraph that is NOT part of a degree of success is being merged into the preceding degree's string, so degree_effects (PFSRD2-Parser-e01u) extracts its damage and attributes it to that degree. In every case the damage is real published damage, but it is not damage that degree's subject takes. Six spells (this list grew to six after fixing an HTML bug — see the last entry): spells/gods__magic/door_to_beyond.json critical_failure 4d6 slashing degree says: "The creature is pulled 20 feet toward the door..." merged text: "...decompressive effects deal 4d6 slashing damage to any creature or object that ends its turn in the door's space" -> save-independent, applies to anyone in the space, not to the crit-failer spells/howl_of_the_wild/gluttonous_growth.json critical_failure 4d6 piercing merged: "When you Sustain this spell, each creature grabbed or restrained ... takes 4d6 piercing damage" -> also applies to success/failure (grabbed) targets, and only on Sustain spells/howl_of_the_wild/summon_stampede.json critical_failure 8d8 bludgeoning merged: a separate **Depart** ability, *Flatten the Earth*, with its OWN basic Reflex save spells/war_of_immortals/final_fate_of_the_locust_host.json critical_failure 5d8 piercing + 5d8 poison merged: a separate **Depart** ability with its own basic Reflex save, hitting enemies in a 60-foot emanation spells/rival_academies/indolent_haze.json critical_failure 6d4 spirit merged: "Any creature in the area who is already unconscious ... takes 6d4 spirit damage" -> hits creatures who were ALREADY unconscious, not the crit-failer. Note the missing space after the period in the merged text ("...unconscious.Any creature...") which is the merge itself showing. spells/war_of_immortals/seize_identity.json critical_failure 2d8 void merged: "The first time each round you Sustain this spell ... the target ages rapidly, taking 2d8 void damage (basic Will save)" -> a Sustain effect with its own save. THIS ONE WAS HIDDEN until 2026-08-17: the source HTML had a stray ">" in the damage type ("2d8 void> damage"), which stopped the extractor matching it. Fixing that HTML typo in pfsrd2-web revealed the misattribution underneath. Worth knowing that a parse artifact was masking a second bug. The shared cause is upstream of degree_effects: the degree's VALUE is absorbing text that follows the degree block. degree_effects only makes it visible, by turning the absorbed prose into structure. Fixing the boundary fixes both the string and the extraction. Compare PFSRD2-Parser-167's routine_results work on hazards, which solved the same shape for hazard routines by bounding a degree at its
separator rather than at the next bold. Found by a per-file review of all 78 changed spell files while staging PR #175's data. All six are held unstaged.
notes:
CORRECTION to the "43 were ALREADY COMMITTED" figure in the note above.

That number came from a script that treated "not in the held list" as "committed", which is wrong -- most of those files were simply UNMODIFIED in the working tree at the time, not part of any commit on feature/hazard-degree-effects.

Accurate accounting, measured against the actual file lists of the three data commits (c2e82f0c0, 7429e9324, 991325726):

  70 spells change under the boundary rules
     4 are in one of those three commits
    25 were held back by the per-file review
    41 were previously CLEAN in the working tree

The substantive point is unchanged and if anything sharper: those 41 are
long-shipped HEAD data whose degree text has been wrong for as long as it has
existed. They were never part of this PR's data commits -- the boundary fix is
correcting the repository's existing content, not something introduced here.

Blast radius of the boundary rules across every parser, all with 0 parse errors:

  spells             70  (4 in my commits)
  monsters           30  (0)
  feats              29  (1)
  npcs                7  (0)
  monster_families    4  (0)
  skills              3  (0)
  hazards             1  (1)

Only 7 files that were committed on this branch changed again, which is the
number that matters for stability: the three data commits did not need to be
revisited.

title: degree_effects extracts a whole affliction stage table into one degree (12 spells)
description:
The affliction parser folds an affliction's stage block into the LAST degree of the spell that inflicts it, so the degree string literally contains the whole stage table. degree_effects (PFSRD2-Parser-e01u) then extracts every die in it and attributes all of them to that one degree.

Example, spells/core_rulebook/purple_worm_sting.json:

  critical_failure text:
    "...afflicted with purple worm venom at stage 2.
     **Stage 1** 3d6 poison damage (1 round)
     **Stage 2** 4d6 poison damage (1 round)
     **Stage 3** 6d6 poison damage (1 round)"

  degree_effects emitted for critical_failure:
    3d6 poison, 4d6 poison, 6d6 poison

A consumer reads that as the critical failure dealing 13d6 poison at once. What the source says is that the critical failure inflicts the affliction AT STAGE 2, and the stage dice apply per round as the affliction progresses.

The extraction is text-faithful — those dice really are inside that degree's string — so this is arguably a modelling question rather than a bug, and it is filed for a decision rather than as a defect.

12 affected files, all spells:
  advanced_players_guide/curse_of_death.json      4d6 + 8d6 + 12d6 negative
  player_core/curse_of_death.json                 4d6 + 8d6 + 12d6 void
  battlecry/blinding_bottle.json                  3d6 + 4d6 + 5d6 + 6d6 poison
  battlecry/blister_bomb.json                     1d6 + 2d6 persistent bleed
  core_rulebook/ghoulish_cravings.json            3d8 negative
  core_rulebook/purple_worm_sting.json            3d6 + 4d6 + 6d6 poison
  core_rulebook/spider_sting.json                 1d4 poison
  player_core/spider_sting.json                   1d4 poison
  pathfinder_160_.../leng_sting.json              2d6 + 3d6 + 4d6 poison
  pathfinder_160_.../linnorm_sting.json           8d6 + 12d6 fire
  pathfinder_160_.../swarming_wasp_stings.json    2d6 + 3d6 poison
  pathfinder_160_.../wyvern_sting.json            5d6 + 6d6 + 8d6 poison

Note blinding_bottle's `success` degree (3d6 poison) IS correct — only the last degree carries the folded table.

Three ways out, in increasing order of work:
 1. Accept it. The values are text-correct and the affliction is separately modelled elsewhere; document the caveat in the schema description.
 2. Stop extracting past the point where the affliction block begins (the first "**Stage 1**" / stage marker in the degree text).
 3. Stop folding the affliction block into the degree at all, and attach it as its own object — which is the real fix, and much larger.

Found by a per-file review of all 78 changed spell files while staging PR #175's data. These 12 are held unstaged pending this decision.

title: Published schemas had properties REMOVED without a rev: equipment x6, creature x5, spell x3
description:
equipment.schema.1.0.json has been rewritten in place 11 times since 2026-03-07, always at schema_version 1.0. Six of those rewrites REMOVED properties from the published contract:

  a122984f1  2026-03-20  parser update
      properties.pfs.enum
  f0236bb6b  2026-03-20  equipment revisions
      equipment_stat_block.properties.pfs.properties.availability
      equipment_stat_block.properties.pfs.properties.note
      (26 key paths in total)
  548984eb1  2026-03-22  fixing area and range for equipment and spells
      definitions.range.properties.value
  a2a908ed8  2026-08-13  data: move item_category/item_subcategory into stat_block
      properties.item_category
      properties.item_subcategory
  b978ee7e3  2026-08-13  schema: enforce item_category on main stat_block via allOf
      properties.stat_block.$ref
  31eedf507  2026-08-15  data: structured weapon damage dice, and executable rune effects
      definitions.rune_effect_modifier  (36 key paths in total)

Under the rule now written into CLAUDE.md and docs/schema-guide.md ("add freely, rev on change"), each of those needed a version bump. Removing or relocating a property a consumer already reads is exactly the breaking case the rule reserves a rev for, and pfsrd2-display is handed files stamped 1.0 that were produced under at least seven mutually incompatible readings of what 1.0 means.

Repro:
  cd pfsrd2-data
  git log --follow --oneline -- equipment.schema.1.0.json
  git show a2a908ed8:equipment.schema.1.0.json | python3 -c "import json,sys; print('item_category' in json.load(sys.stdin)['properties'])"

Found by the schema-consistency reviewer during PR #175 round 2 and independently reproduced by diffing parsed key paths across every revision of the file. NOT caused by #175 — that PR only adds degree_effects, which is a compatible addition and correctly published without a rev.

creature.schema.1.4.json should be checked the same way; the reviewer reported it has been rewritten 11 times, and I have not audited whether any of those were removals.

Decision needed from the maintainer, since both options have a cost:
 1. Rev equipment to 1.1 now, accepting that files already shipped as 1.0 stay ambiguous.
 2. Leave it, and treat 1.0 as "whatever the parser last wrote" for equipment specifically.
Doing nothing silently is the one option the new rule rules out.
notes:
WIDENED after auditing the other published schemas. Equipment is not special — it is just the worst.

Same method (diff parsed key paths across every revision of the published file, counting only paths under .properties. or .definitions.):

  schema                        revisions   with removals
  equipment.schema.1.0.json        11            6
  creature.schema.1.4.json         14            5
  spell.schema.1.0.json             5            3
  hazard.schema.1.0.json           16            1

creature.schema.1.4.json removals:
  0a2b6bbe6  2026-03-20  big pfs fix                       2 paths
  545aeb311  2026-03-22  huge update for enrichment        1
  f23adefd7  2026-03-27  latest tranche of data            4
  aa6230f6e  2026-03-28  lots of license adds              2
  cab64414f  2026-03-28  Merging parsers for abilities    41

spell.schema.1.0.json removals:
  71b4ad502  2026-03-07  some fixing of the schemas        3
  0a2b6bbe6  2026-03-20  big pfs fix                       2
  548984eb1  2026-03-22  fixing area and range             2

hazard.schema.1.0.json removals:
  4f5fe98d4  2026-08-15  hazard attacks, structured stealth  2
  (the maintainer has said hazards are not fully in use yet, so this one is
  probably harmless and is listed only for completeness)

Every one of these stayed at its published version. creature 1.4 and spell 1.0 are both consumed, so the same objection as equipment applies: pfsrd2-display is handed files stamped with a version whose meaning has changed underneath it several times.

Caveat on the numbers, stated rather than buried: a "removal" here is a key path that disappeared between revisions. Some are genuine property deletions (item_category, rune_effect_modifier, pfs.availability); others are refactors where a property MOVED (e.g. item_category relocating into stat_block) and so appear as a removal at the old path and an addition at the new one. A move is still a break for a consumer reading the old path, which is why they are counted, but the six/five/three figures are "paths that stopped existing", not "properties deleted outright". Anyone acting on this should read the individual diffs before deciding severity per case.

title: Equipment degrees are not modelled: activation/save_results/attack_roll miss degree_effects
description:
PFSRD2-Parser-e01u models what a degree of success SAYS as degree_effects[] on the object that carries the degree. It is wired at every writer that goes through universal/ — extract_result_blocks (feats, spells, abilities), _apply_addon (hazard/family/template abilities), creatures._apply_addons, and hazard._extract_routine_results.

equipment.py writes degrees itself and reaches none of them, so two equipment object types keep unmodelled degrees:

  activation    40 degrees whose text carries extractable damage
  save_results  29 degrees whose text carries extractable damage
  attack_roll    1 (weapons/)

Measured by running pfsrd2.enrichment.regex_extractor.extract_all over every degree string under equipment/, weapons/, armor/, shields/, vehicles/ and siege_weapons/ in pfsrd2-data and counting those that come back with a damage object. Reproduce with the script in this ticket's discussion, or:

  grep -l '"subtype": "activation"' -r pfsrd2-data/equipment | head

The fix is the same one-liner used at the other four writers — call extract_degree_effects(obj) once the degrees on that object are final — plus a degree_effects property on activation, save_results and attack_roll in equipment.schema.json and weapon.schema.json. equipment.schema.json already has the degree_effect and attack_damage definitions from e01u; only the property is missing.

Deferred from e01u rather than fixed there because equipment has its own degree-writing code and its own six-type run, so it is a separable change with a separable data diff.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
When equipment starts modelling degrees, pfsrd2/qa/degree_exemptions.unmodelled_outside_the_deferral() has to become bidirectional.

It currently checks one direction only: a content directory that carries unmodelled degrees and is NOT in DEFERRED_DIRS is reported. It cannot see the reverse — the deferral widening INSIDE the deferred set, so more equipment data falls under the guard being switched off.

That asymmetry is acceptable today because the guard is off for all of equipment already, so widening cannot lose coverage that exists. The moment this ticket lands and equipment begins emitting degree_effects, it stops being acceptable: a regression that quietly re-deferred part of equipment would be invisible.

Raised by strategic-fragility-reviewer on PR #175, thread 3807857566.

Two other things in that PR are staged for this ticket:
- pfsrd2/equipment.py's attack_roll carry uses plain DEGREE_FIELDS. It should become DEGREE_FIELDS_WITH_EFFECTS, but ONLY after equipment.schema.json's attack_roll gains a degree_effects property — it is currently additionalProperties: false without one, so switching first ships invalid output. tests/test_degree_exemptions.py::TestTheEquipmentCarryStaysPlain pins this and will fail when the schema changes, which is the intended prompt.
- equipment.py:3767's label_map is the last hand-written copy of the degree names, kept deliberately because it maps DISPLAY labels rather than field names. Merging it with universal.RESULT_LABELS belongs here.

title: Creature parser output is non-deterministic for monsters sharing an output filename (boggard_scout)
description:
Two monster files are regenerated from a different AoN page than the one that produced the committed version, so a full creature run rewrites them with an unrelated creature's data.

  monsters/monster_core/boggard_scout.json
  monsters/pathfinder_game_night_dawn_of_the_frogs_deluxe_adventure/boggard_scout.json

Both AoN pages write to the same two output paths:

  Monsters.aspx.ID_2856  Boggard Scout, Monster Core
  Monsters.aspx.ID_4000  Boggard Scout, Pathfinder Game Night: Dawn of the Frogs

Committed data has monster_core/boggard_scout.json carrying aonid 4000; a run today writes aonid 2856 into it, and swaps the source list, the "more recent version" note, several link aonids, ability text and one saving_throw. Nothing about the diff is a parse improvement — it is simply the other page's content, and whichever page the loop reaches last wins.

Repro:
  PFSRD2-Parser/bin/pf2_run_creatures.sh
  cd pfsrd2-data && git diff monsters/monster_core/boggard_scout.json
  # aonid 4000 -> 2856

Found while verifying PFSRD2-Parser-e01u's creature diff: these were the only two of 131 changed files whose diff contained no degree_effects and was not already explained by PFSRD2-Parser-r0wc.

This is the creature-side instance of PFSRD2-Parser-8sgb (same defect in the equipment parser: two items sharing an output filename). Fix should probably be shared — a deterministic tie-break, or distinct filenames when two pages collide, rather than last-writer-wins.
notes:
NOT A BUG — closing. My premise was wrong.

The maintainer: "last one writes isn't a defect. Archive of Nethys adds new objects as the same thing comes out in a different book, and it's meant to override the lower id."

So two AoN pages writing to one output filename is the DESIGNED behaviour, not a collision. When Paizo reprints a creature in a new book, AoN publishes a new object with a new (higher) ID, and the newer object is meant to supersede the older one. Both output copies carrying the newest version is the correct end state.

Checked against the corpus after a full creature run:

  monsters/monster_core/boggard_scout.json                       aonid 4000
  monsters/pathfinder_game_night_.../boggard_scout.json          aonid 4000

Both carry 4000 (Dawn of the Frogs, the newer object) rather than 2856 (Monster Core). That is the override working. What I reported as "unexplained churn" was a mid-run snapshot: 2856 is written first, 4000 second, and I looked between the two writes.

One narrow thing I do NOT want to assert but will leave here in case it matters to whoever reads this next: the higher ID wins because the driver iterates `ls Monsters.aspx.ID_*.html`, which sorts LEXICALLY. That coincides with numeric order only while colliding IDs have the same digit count — ID_999 sorts after ID_1000. I have not checked whether any colliding pair straddles a digit-count boundary, so this may be a non-issue; it is recorded as a question, not a finding.
close_reason: Not a bug: AoN's newer object is meant to override the lower ID; both output copies correctly carry the newest version

title: extract_bold_fields drops published values: linked labels and table header cells
description:
universal/universal.py::extract_bold_fields writes `section[key] = value` with no emptiness check and no _set_once. Two distinct losses follow, and the SECOND is the larger one. On the seven parsers that run remove_empty_fields before validation, an empty value written as "" is then deleted, reproducing the "no trace at all" outcome of PFSRD2-Parser-mgz4 by a different route. creatures.py and npcs skip that pass, which is the only reason any of it is visible in shipped data. A THIRD copy of the same logic, with neither guard, is at pfsrd2/creatures.py::_apply_addons. == HALF ONE: DUPLICATE LABELS (the bigger half) == Each write clobbers the last, so an ability publishing several Damage in
  • items keeps only the final one. Measured in-process over all 3644 monster files: 11 files, 63 collisions, NONE legitimate. shade.json (ID_4541) loses 21 of 22 planar variants' damage; one formula survives, 1d8+2 imp.json (ID_109) ships damage [{formula: "1"}] while 1d10, 1d6-1 and "plus 1d4 poison" occur ZERO times anywhere in the file — consumed out of the text as well An earlier version of this ticket told implementers NOT to add a duplicate-label assert, claiming it fires on 9 legitimate creature files because ID_57 has jaws and claw attacks each with their own Damage. That was wrong and is retracted. ID_57 produces no duplicate at all here — Strikes are consumed by the attack parser before extract_bold_fields sees them. The claim came from reading only the first assert hit per file and then inspecting a file whose first hit was something else entirely. == HALF TWO: EMPTY VALUES == Measured with a temporary emptiness assert across ALL EIGHT consumers: creatures 4 (2 already fixed as HTML bugs, pfsrd2-web 21eae6bf06) hazards 5 npcs 0 feats 0 monster_families 0 monster_templates 0 skills 0 monster_abilities 0 The two remaining creature cases are code bugs: 1. LINKED LABEL — Monsters.aspx.ID_57 (brain_collector) Saving Throw DC 26 Fortitude; The bold sits INSIDE an , so bold.next_sibling is None and the value walk starts past the end. hazard.py handles this deliberately via _is_label_bold, which returns True for an `a` whose child is a `b`; extract_bold_fields has no equivalent. Ships an empty save with the DC stranded in prose. 2. TABLE HEADER CELL READ AS A LABEL — Monsters.aspx.ID_3304 (scroungefeather) The header cell's Effect collides with the ability's real Effect label. The table cell wins, writes "", and the real paragraph — "The scroungefeather uses an Interact action to grab an item with its beak..." — is absent from the JSON entirely. monster_family.py already guards this shape at its own call site; extract_bold_fields does not. The five hazard cases lose whole stat-block fields rather than one value: ID_269 Spiral Seal empty Reset ID_390 Guardian Mural empty Routine ID_549 Electric Fence empty Routine ID_551 Paralysis Trap empty Disable — the Disable instructions ship as two bogus abilities named "Thievery" and "Arcana" ID_622 label not yet identified == WHY NOT FIXED IN PR #170 == That PR guards _apply_addon, a different entry point with zero live instances. Everything here touches extract_bold_fields, which all eight parsers use, so it needs its own full-corpus validation rather than riding along on a one-line assert.
    d4Item Effect
acceptance_criteria: extract_bold_fields (1) asserts rather than writing an empty value, (2) refuses to silently overwrite a label it has already written, (3) handles a linked Label the way hazard.py does, and (4) ignores bold inside tables. All eight consuming parsers run clean. shade.json carries all 22 planar variants' damage, imp.json's 1d10 and 1d4 poison are present, scroungefeather's Effect paragraph is in its JSON, and Paralysis Trap's Disable text is a Disable field rather than two abilities named Thievery and Arcana. The same treatment is applied to or explicitly ruled out for the third copy at creatures.py::_apply_addons.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-16 — the do-not warning previously in this ticket was WRONG, and would have steered an implementer away from the check that finds the largest loss here. It has been removed. What follows replaces it. I had written: "do NOT add a duplicate-label assert alongside the emptiness one; it fires on 9 legitimate creature files — ID_57 has jaws and claw attacks each with its own Damage." That is false, twice over: 1. ID_57 produces NO duplicate at all in extract_bold_fields. Its jaws/claw Damage pair never reaches this function in one call, because Strikes are consumed by the attack parser first. The example I cited does not reproduce. How I got it wrong: my probe reported only the FIRST assert hit per file. I read "9 DUPE Damage" in aggregate, then opened ID_57 — whose first hit was actually MEASURE-EMPTY 'Saving Throw' — and generalised from the wrong file's HTML. 2. The duplicates are real losses, not legitimate shapes: 11 files, 63 collisions, none legitimate. All are single abilities publishing several Damage in
  • items, where each write clobbers the last. shade.json (ID_4541) loses 21 of 22 planar variants' damage — one formula survives, 1d8+2. imp.json (ID_109) ships damage [{formula: "1"}] while 1d10, 1d6-1 and "plus 1d4 poison" appear NOWHERE in the file, having been consumed out of the text as well. Verified: the string "1d10" occurs 0 times in the shipped imp.json. So the duplicate check belongs in this ticket's scope alongside the emptiness check, and it is the higher-value half by an order of magnitude — 63 lost values against 4 empty ones. SCOPE CORRECTION: the emptiness measurement in the original description covered only creatures and NPCs, which is 2 of the 8 parsers that reach extract_bold_fields. Re-measured across the rest: hazards 5 files, and 0 in monster_families, monster_templates, skills and monster_abilities. The hazard cases are the worst shape found so far, because they lose whole stat-block fields rather than one value: Hazards ID_269 'Spiral Seal' empty Reset Hazards ID_390 'Guardian Mural' empty Routine Hazards ID_549 'Electric Fence' empty Routine Hazards ID_551 'Paralysis Trap' empty Disable — its Disable instructions ship as two bogus abilities named "Thievery" and "Arcana" Hazards ID_622 (fifth file, label not yet identified) Corpus total for the emptiness half: 4 creature files (2 already fixed in pfsrd2-web 21eae6bf06) + 5 hazards + 0 elsewhere. FEATS MEASUREMENT COMPLETE (it was still running when the census above was written): feats 7706 files, 0 hits. So the emptiness half is exactly 4 creature files + 5 hazards across all 8 consumers, of which 2 creature files are already fixed in pfsrd2-web 21eae6bf06.

title: skill_check and action_check as two object types; secondary DCs are unstructured
description:
Degree-of-success text names DCs that are NOT saving throws, and nothing captures any of them structurally.

DEVON'S DESIGN CALL: a skill check probably wants a new object type, mostly the same as save_dc, called something like skill_check, carrying the skill (e.g. Acrobatics).

MEASURED — 20 secondary DCs inside degree fields across hazards/families/templates:

   10  bare "DC 25"      the check type appears later in the sentence, not adjacent to the DC
    5  save              "DC 33 Reflex save to avoid", "DC 32 basic Reflex save"
    2  skill check       "DC 30 Acrobatics check"          <- needs the new type
    2  flat check        "DC 5 flat check or they..."
    1  "DC 45 checks to Escape from"

Examples:
   test_of_agility        Tilt and Roll     success           "DC 30 Acrobatics check"
   test_of_agility        Tilt and Roll     failure           "DC 33 Reflex save"
   disorienting_illusions Disorient         critical_failure  "DC 5 flat check"
   the_putrid_rise        Vomit             critical_failure  "DC 32 basic Reflex save"
   collapsing_cell        Collapse          failure           "DC 25"  (type stated later in the sentence)

So three shapes are in play, and they are genuinely different things:
   - saving throw  -> existing save_dc, save_type Fort/Ref/Will
   - flat check    -> existing save_dc convention (a flat check occupies the same slot as Will/Fort — Devon, see tys6)
   - skill check   -> NEW object type, same shape as save_dc plus the skill name

The bare "DC 25" majority is the hard part: the DC and the check type are separated by prose, so a naive regex on the DC will not tell you which of the three it is. Whatever is built needs to fail loudly rather than guess — misclassifying a skill check as a save produces plausible-looking wrong data.

These are SECONDARY checks described inside an outcome, not the ability's own save, so they must not be merged into ability["saving_throw"]. Cloud of Ashes' own save is DC 30 Fort and is correct; its failure text separately names a DC 5 flat check.

NOT a regression from PR #167 — verified that zero of these were structured before that change either.
design:
DESIGN -- SETTLED (Devon, 2026-08-21). Supersedes every sketch above.

TWO OBJECT TYPES, not one object with this-or-that optionality:

    skill_check  = { dc, skill }             # source names a skill, no action
    action_check = { dc, action, skill? }    # source names an action

action is ALWAYS present on an action_check. skill on an action_check is a
REFINEMENT -- "this instance uses this one of the action's permitted skills" --
never an alternative to action. So there is no "one of these two must be set"
rule to enforce anywhere: each type's required fields are simply required.

The action carries its own permitted-skills list (PFSRD2-Parser-q3pk). An
action_check does not duplicate that list; it records only the narrowing, and
only when the source states one.

Why the refinement is kept rather than deriving skill from the action: where an
action permits exactly one skill (Disable a Device -> Thievery) the skill is
recoverable and the field is simply absent. Where it permits several it is not.
Escape allows Athletics, Thievery, Acrobatics and an unarmed attack modifier,
so "a DC 25 Athletics check to Escape" states something the action alone does
not, and Escape is the most common action named in creature ability text.

MEASURED against the 28 misfiled DCs found in the enrichment cache:

    12  action only          "the DC to Escape ... is 40"          -> action_check
     8  action + skill       "DC 43 Acrobatics check to Maneuver
                              in Flight"                           -> action_check + skill
     2  skill only           "DC 30 Acrobatics check"              -> skill_check
     9  NEITHER              bare "DC 25", type named later         -> emit nothing

"DC N <Skill> check to <Action>" is a regular published shape, not an accident:

    "DC 43 Acrobatics check to Maneuver in Flight"     Whiffling
    "DC 18 Thievery check to Disable a Device"         Modular Arms
    "DC 14 Thievery check to Disable a Device"         Wind-Up

THE 9 "NEITHER" CASES fit neither type and must emit nothing rather than guess.
That is a third of the sample, so this split recovers ~19 of the 28 initially,
not all of them. Failing loudly is the point -- guessing is what filed these
under saving_throw to begin with. Do not add a dc-only fallback object to close
the gap; that recreates the untyped DC this ticket exists to remove.
acceptance_criteria:
skill_check and action_check exist as distinct object types with their own subtypes.

action_check always carries an action; its skill field is present only when the source names a specific skill, and is never used as a substitute for the action.

The 19 classifiable DCs from the enrichment evidence (12 action-only, 8 action+skill, 2 skill-only; Whiffling, Modular Arms, Wind-Up, Impaling Charge, Web Tether, Poison Tooth among them) parse into the right type.

The 9 unclassifiable bare-DC cases emit nothing and are flagged, not guessed into either type.

No skill/action DC is written into ability[saving_throw] any more.

Unit tests cover: action-only, action+skill refinement, skill-only, and the bare-DC case emitting nothing.
notes:
NEW EVIDENCE 2026-08-21, from validating every LLM-sourced enrichment cache.

This is not only a degree-text problem. 28 ability records in the enrichment
DB had a skill/action DC filed under ability["saving_throw"] with
save_type=None -- the field that is supposed to hold Fort/Ref/Will/flat.

  "Removing the tooth safely requires a successful DC 26 check to
   Administer First Aid"                                    Poison Tooth
  "The DC to Escape or Force Open the web is 30"            Web Tether
  "flight in the emanation requires a successful DC 43
   Acrobatics check to Maneuver in Flight"                  Whiffling
  "the DC to do so is 40, rather than Cuetzmonquali's..."   Impaling Charge

The grounding filters added in 29beaaf now DROP these rather than misfile
them, so the corruption is stopped -- but the data is simply lost until this
ticket lands. Dropping is the floor, not the fix.

MEASURED -- of the 28, the text names a known skill action in 11:

     3  Administer First Aid   (Medicine)
     3  Force Open             (Athletics)
     3  Disable a Device       (Thievery)
     2  Maneuver in Flight     (Acrobatics)
     2  Grapple                (Athletics)
     2  Perform                (Performance)
     1  Climb                  (Athletics)
     1  Balance                (Acrobatics)
     1  Repair                 (Crafting)

These are eminently linkable: the skills corpus already publishes 73 distinct
skill actions as skill.actions[] with subtype "skill_action", carrying
action_type, traits, sample_tasks and links. So skill_check should carry
enough to resolve to one of those, not just a bare skill name string.

IMPORTANT -- two different corpora are involved, and only one exists:

  skill actions   Force Open, Grapple, Climb, Administer First Aid ...
                  live in skills/*/*.json under skill.actions[]. Present.

  general Actions Escape is NOT a skill action. It is game-obj "Actions",
                  aonid 79, because it can be attempted with Acrobatics,
                  Athletics, or an unarmed attack modifier. The skills files
                  reference it only as a link. There is no actions/ directory
                  in pfsrd2-data and no bin/pf2_run_actions.sh -- the Actions
                  corpus has never been parsed. See the new ticket for that.

Escape is the single most common shape in the remaining 17 unmatched cases
(Impaling Charge, Clockwork String, Encase -- all "grabbed, Escape DC N"), so
skill_check needs to model a check that resolves to an Action, not only to a
skill. Recommend the object carry the game-obj/aonid pair the rest of the
pipeline uses, so it can point at either corpus.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

FEED THE LINKS TO THE LLM (Devon, 2026-08-21).

The links are not only for deterministic resolution -- they are context the
extractor should be given, because they help with the saves too.

Today they are NOT given. pfsrd2/ability_enrichment.py builds the LLM input as

    combined = f"{text} {effect}".strip()

and passes that. But `links` is a sibling top-level key on the same ability
object and never reaches the model. For Whiffling the model is asked to
classify "DC 43" while being denied the two facts that settle it:

    {"alt": "Acrobatics", "aonid": 1, "game-obj": "Skills", ...}
    {"alt": "Maneuver in Flight", "aonid": 30, "game-obj": "Actions", ...}

A Skills or Actions link is strong evidence the DC is NOT a save, and the
absence of one alongside a named Fort/Ref/Will is evidence that it is. The
game-obj values are a small closed vocabulary (Skills, Actions, Rules,
Conditions, Traits, ...), so this is cheap, structured context rather than
more prose.

Do this as a measured change, not an assumed improvement. Every prompt
revision on the damage extractor was measured and four of four were worse --
see the comment above the damage prompt in llm_config.toml and the
filter-dont-instruct memory. Adding grounding CONTEXT is a different kind of
change from adding a rule, but it still gets A/B'd against the corpus before
it ships.

Note the ordering constraint: there is nowhere to PUT a skill/action result
until skill_check and action_check exist, so the payoff for classification
lands with this ticket. Any measured gain for plain saves can ship earlier.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-19: the census below was measured before the degree-boundary
fixes in PR #175 and is superseded. Ten published schema descriptions point
readers at this ticket for the exact figures, so the stale numbers were being
cited as authoritative.

CURRENT MEASUREMENT (2026-08-19, PR #175 HEAD), DC occurrences inside degree text:

    160 total
     64 Escape DC
     44 saving throw
     44 flat check          <- this ticket
      7 skill check
      1 naming no check at all   (monsters/monster_core_2/ravener.json)

The total moved 163 -> 160 because the degree boundary rules in
universal/universal.py decide how much text a degree contains, and tightening
them shrank the corpus this counts. Re-derive before quoting: any change to
stop_at_paragraph, the last-degree bound, or _continues_past_a_break moves it
again. That is precisely why the published schemas no longer carry a tally of
their own.

title: Model flat checks as a boolean on save_dc, not as save_type
description:
A flat check is a d20 rolled with no bonuses — it describes the TYPE OF ROLL, not a saving throw. Modelling it as save_type="Flat Check" conflates a roll type with the Fort/Ref/Will axis.

DEVON'S DECISION: a boolean on save_dc that can be set to true is an acceptable answer.

    {"dc": 5, "flat_check": true, "subtype": "save_dc", "text": "DC 5 flat check"}

rather than

    {"dc": 5, "save_type": "Flat Check", ...}

SCOPE (measured against shipped data)

  save_dc objects currently carrying save_type="Flat Check":
      monsters            212 objects / 167 files
      npcs                 43 objects /  40 files
      monster_families     13 objects /  10 files
      monster_templates     1 object  /   1 file
      TOTAL               269 objects / 218 files

  The mapping lives in universal/creatures.py (~line 300): "flat" -> "Flat Check".

WORK
 1. add `flat_check` (boolean) to the save_dc definition, copied byte-identically into every schema that defines save_dc (creature, hazard, affliction, spell, equipment... check docs/schema-guide.md for the full list)
 2. stop emitting save_type="Flat Check"; set flat_check=true instead
 3. decide whether save_type should be absent or retained when flat_check is true — a flat check has no save axis, so absent is probably right
 4. full re-run of every affected content type; this touches 218 files of shipped data
 5. tell the pfsrd2-data-api / pfsrd2-automation consumers: docs/affliction-data-consumer-guide.md and docs/hazard-data-consumer-guide.md both document save_dc

SEPARATE BUT RELATED (do not conflate)
17 abilities name a DC ONLY inside degree-of-success text ("must succeed at a DC 5 flat check", "DC 30 Acrobatics", "DC 32 basic") and NONE of them capture it structurally. That is a secondary check described within an outcome — it is not the ability's own save, so it must not be merged into the ability's saving_throw. It needs its own home. Long-standing gap, not introduced by PR #167.

Found while reviewing the monster_family diff on PR #167: dragon_cinder's Cloud of Ashes keeps its real save (DC 30 Fort); what disappeared was a save_dc hanging off a BOGUS "Failure" ability, carrying save_type="Flat Check".
